title: Rick Rubin on Finding Your Life's Work
speaker: David Senra & Rick Rubin

sentences.en: Five years ago, I read this biography of you.
sentences.zh: 五年前，我读了你的这本传记。

sentences.en: It's called In the Studio. You and I were just talking about it before we started recording.
sentences.zh: 书名叫《In the Studio》。刚才录音前我们还在聊这本书。

sentences.en: One of my favorite ideas that I took away from that book that I think about probably every week is this concept that you have that less is more, but to get less, you have to do more.
sentences.zh: 我从书中收获的最喜欢的观点之一，也是我几乎每周都会思考的，就是你提到的那个概念：少即是多，但要做到“少”，你反而得做更多。

sentences.en: Can you talk a little bit about that? Yeah.
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这一点吗？好的。

sentences.en: If you're stacking a lot of things on top of each other, each one of those things becomes less important.
sentences.zh: 如果你堆砌了太多东西，每一项的重要性都会被稀释。

sentences.en: So if you have 10 things, each one of them is one-tenth as important as one by itself.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有10样东西，每一项的重要性只有单独存在时的十分之一。

sentences.en: So if you're making something and you want the least amount involved, those things have to be really critically curated because they're doing the work of everything and nothing is hidden.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你在创作，并且希望参与其中的元素最少，那么这些元素必须经过极其严苛的筛选，因为它们要承担起所有的表现任务，而且没有任何东西是可以被隐藏的。

sentences.en: It's why it's not as easy as it sounds to do less. but it it when you see it you can get the personality i'll give you an example with guitars if you a lot of recordings are made where the guitarist plays and then they double it and triple it and they create this like wall of guitars and when you when there's a wall of guitars you hear guitar but you don't hear someone playing guitar you just hear guitar It becomes more generic.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么“做减法”并不像听起来那么容易。但当你真正做到时，你就能感受到那种个性。我举个吉他的例子：很多录音作品里，吉他手弹完一遍，又叠录两三遍，创造出一堵“吉他墙”。当出现“吉他墙”时，你听到的是吉他声，却听不到有人在弹吉他，你听到的只是吉他本身，这让作品变得平庸了。

sentences.en: When one person plays it and you can hear their fingers on the strings, it's got more personality.
sentences.zh: 当只有一个人在弹奏，你能听到他手指在琴弦上的摩擦声时，它就有了更多的个性。

sentences.en: It's more human. And I tend to look for those things where it's the singular essence shows through.
sentences.zh: 它更具人性。我倾向于寻找那些能展现出独特本质的东西。

sentences.en: Well, I'm always surprised about people that do great things.
sentences.zh: 我总是对那些成就卓越的人感到惊讶。

sentences.en: I think especially from people on the outside.
sentences.zh: 尤其是从局外人的视角来看。

sentences.en: It's like the amount of volume that goes into it before you're presented with their finished work.
sentences.zh: 在最终作品呈现给你之前，他们投入的精力简直不可思议。

sentences.en: I know like you start you know you're obsessed with music when you're a teenager you start Def Jam in your dorm room you're like 18 years old what was the first example was it L.O.
sentences.zh: 我知道你十几岁时就痴迷于音乐，在宿舍里创办了Def Jam，那时你才18岁。第一个例子是谁？是LL Cool J吗？是谁让你意识到：哇，原来创作一件伟大的艺术品、一个伟大的产品或一张伟大的专辑，背后需要付出这么多努力？我当时从未想过这些，因为那就像是一种使命，一种热爱，我甚至没把它当作工作，我只是想做这些东西。

sentences.en: Cool J like who was the first example you're like wow there's a lot more work that goes into making a great piece of art great product great album than I ever knew I never thought about it because it was it was like a mission and a love and I didn't think of it even as work it was just what I wanted to do is make these things.
sentences.zh: 所以，需要付出大量努力这一事实，根本不在我的考虑范围内。

sentences.en: So the fact that it took a lot of work wasn't, it wasn't even in, it wasn't in consideration at all.
sentences.zh: 你18、19岁的时候，是不是整天都在搞音乐？

sentences.en: When you were 18 years old, 19 years old, it was just all music all the time?
sentences.zh: 是的，作为一个乐迷，我一直在听音乐。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's just, as a fan I listened to music all the time.
sentences.zh: 我爱上了它。我想尽一切办法参与其中。那时嘻哈音乐刚在纽约兴起。

sentences.en: I fell in love with it. I wanted to be involved in whatever way that I could. hip-hop was just starting in New York City.
sentences.zh: 它当时完全是一个地下运动。

sentences.en: It was still a totally underground movement.
sentences.zh: 所以你唯一能听到它的地方，就是我上学时市中心的一家俱乐部。

sentences.en: So the only place you could hear it was at one club downtown where I was going to school.
sentences.zh: 当时只有那一家俱乐部能听到嘻哈音乐，而且一周只有一次。

sentences.en: There was only one club that you could hear hip-hop and that was once a week.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，它只存在于布朗克斯、布鲁克林，其实也就是在社区中心和户外派对上。

sentences.en: But other than that, it was only in, it was in the Bronx, it was in Brooklyn, but really just in like community centers and outdoor parties.
sentences.zh: 那是一种地下的、不被看好的音乐。

sentences.en: It was underground and not well thought of kind of music.
sentences.zh: 那是街头音乐。我每周都会去那家俱乐部听音乐。

sentences.en: It was street music. And I would go to this club every week and hear the music.
sentences.zh: 那时市面上只有几张嘻哈唱片，都是12英寸单曲，没有专辑，只有单曲。

sentences.en: And at that time, there would be a few hip hop records coming out, 12-inch singles, no albums, only 12-inch singles.
sentences.zh: 可能每两三周才会出一张新唱片。

sentences.en: And there'd be maybe one new record every two or three weeks.
sentences.zh: 仅此而已。我会每周去俱乐部听音乐，然后买下那几周才出一张的单曲。

sentences.en: And that's all there was. and I would go to the club every week, hear the music there, and then I would buy the one single that would come out every few weeks.
sentences.zh: 但这些单曲并不能代表俱乐部里的那种能量。

sentences.en: And the singles didn't represent what the energy in the club was.
sentences.zh: 我想感受那种俱乐部的能量。

sentences.en: And I wanted to feel that energy of the club.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始制作，我制作的第一张唱片叫《It's Yours》。

sentences.en: So I started, the first record I made was called It's Yours.
sentences.zh: 制作它的目的，就是想把俱乐部里的那种能量捕捉到唱片里。

sentences.en: And the purpose of that was I was just trying to capture the energy of the club on record.
sentences.zh: 我当时对录音一窍不通。

sentences.en: And I didn't know anything about recording.
sentences.zh: 我不是专业人士，我只是个孩子。正因为我不知道自己在做什么，才让它保持了嘻哈音乐最真实的样貌。

sentences.en: I wasn't a professional. I was a kid. The fact that I didn't know what I was doing allowed it to be true to what hip hop was.
sentences.zh: 而当时市面上那些稀稀拉拉的12英寸单曲，都是由制作其他类型音乐的专业人士制作的，他们并不是嘻哈圈内人。所以，一个有经验的局外人在制作他们心目中的“嘻哈”，但如果你去过俱乐部，你就知道真正的嘻哈是什么样的。俱乐部里的音乐非常精简，就是搓碟、鼓点、鼓机和说唱，而我做的唱片就是那样，不像那些由制作其他流派的人做出来的东西。

sentences.en: Whereas all of the records that were coming out, the few and far between 12-inch singles every few weeks, they were made by professionals who made other kinds of music they weren't made by hip-hop people so an outsider with experience was making what they thought hip-hop was but if you went to the club you knew what it really was and the club was very stripped down and it was scratching breakbeats drum machines and rapping and that's what the records were the ones that were produced by people producing other or making other genres of music?
sentences.zh: 是因为修饰太多了吗？感觉很假吗？

sentences.en: Was it like too much polish? Was it like fake?
sentences.zh: 你会怎么描述它和你在俱乐部里听到的区别？

sentences.en: How would you describe the difference from what you're hearing in the club?
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上是你的机会，你进入这个领域的途径。

sentences.en: So this is like your opportunity, essentially, your way into this.
sentences.zh: 这些唱片就像是当时那个场景的纪录片。

sentences.en: The records are like a documentary of this scene that was going on.
sentences.zh: 而那个时期所有其他的记录都无法代表那个场景。

sentences.en: And all of the other documents of that period weren't representative of the scene.
sentences.zh: 它们代表的是别的东西，是那种好莱坞式的专业版本，但那根本不是真相。

sentences.en: They were representative of something else, the professional, like the Hollywood version of it. but that's not what it was.
sentences.zh: 这是你发行的第一张单曲吗？它卖了大概10万张，还是说那是同一张？

sentences.en: Is this the first signal you put out? It sold like 100,000 copies, or is that the same one?
sentences.zh: 对，差不多。卖得很好。

sentences.en: Yeah, something like that. It sold a lot.
sentences.zh: 我是说，在那个世界的唱片里，它花了不少时间。

sentences.en: I mean, for a record in that world, it took a long time.
sentences.zh: 可能花了18个月才卖出10万张，但在18个月里卖了10万张，这已经是一个热门作品了，对于一种永远不会在电台播放、没人听也没人喜欢的音乐来说，这已经是极限了。事实上，当时大多数非嘻哈乐迷甚至不承认它是音乐。

sentences.en: It probably took 18 months to sell 100,000, but over 18 months sold about 100,000, and it was a hit, as much of a hit could be, in something that would never be on the radio and the kind of music that nobody listened to or liked. as a matter of fact, back then, most people who were not hip hop fans didn't even acknowledge it as music.
sentences.zh: 它就是这么小众。他们觉得那是什么？

sentences.en: That's how far it was. What did they think it was?
sentences.zh: 不知道。不过猫王和摇滚乐刚出现时也是这样。

sentences.en: Don't know. It was the same thing though with Elvis and rock and roll.
sentences.zh: 大人们也不承认那是音乐。

sentences.en: The grownups didn't acknowledge that as music.
sentences.zh: 那只是他们不知道是什么的某种怪东西。

sentences.en: It was just some other thing that they didn't know what it was.
sentences.zh: 它就是这么陌生。你18、19岁时，已经在研究更早期的音乐了吗？

sentences.en: That's how foreign it was. When you were 18, 19 years old, were you already studying older versions of music?
sentences.zh: 你当时已经在回溯了吗？我一直都在听。

sentences.en: Did you, you already going back? I always listened.
sentences.zh: 任何我喜欢的音乐，我都想听听那个我喜欢的人，他们听过什么，喜欢什么。

sentences.en: Anything I liked, I wanted to hear everything that the person that I liked, everything they listened to that they liked.
sentences.zh: 我总是想去探究。我在看传记时也是这样。

sentences.en: I always wanted to understand. I do the same thing with biographies.
sentences.zh: 是的。我想了解更多，我会找一些人，比如Steve Jobs，我觉得他很有趣。

sentences.en: Yeah. So I want to know more about this, but I'll find somebody that, you know, like Steve Jobs, for example, I find him very interesting.
sentences.zh: 我会读他的传记。然后这些书里每一本都会提到大概六个，甚至十几个其他人。

sentences.en: I'd read a biography of him. And then every single one of these books, they'll talk about like half a dozen, maybe a dozen people.
sentences.zh: 我就想：那是谁？我不认识这个人。

sentences.en: And I'm like, who's that? I don't know this guy.
sentences.zh: 然后我会去查参考书目，通常能找到关于那些启发了他们的人的书。

sentences.en: And I'll go in the bibliography and usually find books about the people that inspired them.
sentences.zh: 我也是。你还记得第一次这么做是什么时候吗？

sentences.en: Same. Do you remember the first time you did that?
sentences.zh: 比如，你当时对哪个乐队或艺术家特别感兴趣，然后想去查查是谁启发了他们？

sentences.en: Like, who were you like, I'm really interested in this band or this artist.
sentences.zh: 一直都是这样。或者另一种情况是，我第一次听到某样东西时。

sentences.en: Let me find out who they were inspired by.
sentences.zh: 我记得第一次听到MC5，那是60年代底特律的一个乐队，算是原始朋克摇滚乐队。

sentences.en: It's always been the case. Or the other version of it is, it's like it, where I would hear something for the first time.
sentences.zh: 他们在朋克摇滚之前，但有朋克的能量。

sentences.en: I can remember the first time I heard the MC5, which is a band from Detroit in the 1960s, kind of a proto-punk rock band.
sentences.zh: 我听了之后觉得太酷了。

sentences.en: They're before punk rock, but it has punk energy.
sentences.zh: 然后我记得去了二手唱片店，因为二手店里有所有酷的旧货，店员对音乐最了解。

sentences.en: And I heard that, and it was really cool.
sentences.zh: 所以你会在二手唱片店花上几个小时，和店员聊天。

sentences.en: And then I remember going to a used record store because the used record store had all the cool older stuff, and they knew the most about music.
sentences.zh: 就像我们听说Quentin Tarantino在录像带店工作一样，那些真正热爱某样东西的人周围总是有海量的信息。

sentences.en: So you spend hours in used record stores and just talking to the people who work there.
sentences.zh: 我记得他们说，如果你喜欢MC5，那你应该听听Iggy and the Stooges。

sentences.en: Same like we've heard Quentin Tarantino working in a video shop and just there's so much information around the people who really love this thing.
sentences.zh: 然后我听了Stooges，心想：噢，我也爱这个。

sentences.en: And I remember they said, well, if you like the MC5, you might want to check out Iggy and the Stooges.
sentences.zh: 那也是底特律的，同一个时期，同一个场景。

sentences.en: And then I listened to the Stooges like, oh, I love this too.
sentences.zh: 那真是很棒的音乐。所以要么是我自己发现喜欢的音乐，要么是启发了我所爱音乐的音乐。

sentences.en: And that was another also Detroit, same time frame, same scene.
sentences.zh: 这两者我都会一直去追寻。

sentences.en: And it was great music. So it would either be. music like the music that I found that I liked or music that inspired the music that I liked.
sentences.zh: 我总是思考动机，我总是想知道人们为什么要做他们正在做的事。

sentences.en: Both of those were things I would always pursue.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们做事的动机，他们选择进入某个职业的原因，真的很重要。

sentences.en: I always think like the motivations, I always want to know why people are doing what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 你当时以为音乐只能是个爱好？

sentences.en: I think the motivations of what they're doing, the reason that they go into their chosen profession is really important.
sentences.zh: 比如你觉得你得找份正职，然后才能搞音乐？

sentences.en: You thought music was going to be like a hobby.
sentences.zh: 我不知道把它当职业是可能的。

sentences.en: Like you were going to have to get a day job and then just do music.
sentences.zh: 是的。你能谈谈这个吗？好的。我以为我会有一份普通的工作。

sentences.en: I didn't know it was possible to be a job.
sentences.zh: 我不认识任何以音乐为生的人，我无法想象那样的生活。

sentences.en: Yeah. Can you talk about that? Yeah. I thought I would have a regular job.
sentences.zh: 我没有任何背景，家里也没有人是艺术家，所以那不是一个现实的期望。

sentences.en: I didn't know anyone who did music professionally or I couldn't imagine it.
sentences.zh: 所以我以为我会像往常一样热爱音乐。

sentences.en: I didn't have any, and no one in my family was an artist, so it wasn't a realistic expectation.
sentences.zh: 如果我想，我可以参与其中制作音乐，但我得有一份工作来养活自己。

sentences.en: So I thought I'd love music the way I always have.
sentences.zh: 所以我没觉得音乐能支撑我的生活。

sentences.en: I could participate and make music if I want, but I would have a job to support myself.
sentences.zh: 你当时在一个乐队里，对吧？我想你弹吉他。

sentences.en: So I didn't think that that was possible for music to support my life.
sentences.zh: 在一个朋克乐队，所以非常基础。

sentences.en: You were in a band, right? You played, I think, guitar.
sentences.zh: 是的，然后是DJ。我还是有点困惑。

sentences.en: In a punk rock band, so it was very rudimentary.
sentences.zh: 你能试着解释一下，是什么路径让你走到了现在这个非常独特的地位吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, and then DJ. I'm still a little confused.
sentences.zh: 是的，我只是始终追随当时我感兴趣的东西。

sentences.en: Can you try to explain the path that led you to this very singular position that you have now?
sentences.zh: 所以当朋克摇滚出现时，嗯，在朋克之前其实是重金属。

sentences.en: Yeah, I just always followed what was interesting to me at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时的重金属其实更像是硬摇滚，而不是我们现在认为的重金属。

sentences.en: So when punk rock came along, well, first before punk rock would be heavy metal.
sentences.zh: 比如Aerosmith、ACDC、Ted Nugent，这些是我13、14岁时竞技场摇滚的中流砥柱，我喜欢那种音乐，然后我买了一把吉他试着跟着弹，结果不太好。但当朋克摇滚出现时，我更容易跟着弹，因为音乐更基础。

sentences.en: Heavy metal at that time was really more like hard rock than what we think of now as heavy metal.
sentences.zh: 但你是怎么从那儿走到DJ这条路的？

sentences.en: So it would be Aerosmith, ACDC, Ted Nugent. those were kind of the mainstays of what arena rock was like when I was 13 or 14 years old and I loved that music and then I got a guitar and tried to play along and it didn't it didn't go well but then when punk rock came along I could it was easier for me to play along because it was more basic music.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的事是我在高中时对嘻哈产生了兴趣，有一些孩子——我高中里没人喜欢朋克，只有我——但有一些孩子喜欢嘻哈。

sentences.en: But how do you go from that to, is DJ the next route in?
sentences.zh: 这又是发生在嘻哈非常、非常、非常早期的阶段。

sentences.en: The next thing that happened was in my interest in hip hop in high school, there were some kids, no one in my high school liked punk rock except me, but there were some kids who liked hip hop.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这还是保守了。我是说，在嘻哈的开端，因为我记得读过关于Def Jam早期创立的内容。

sentences.en: And this was, again, in the very, very, very early days of hip hop.
sentences.zh: 然后我总是喜欢在读书时写下我所处的年份，然后查一下那个人出生的年份。

sentences.en: I think that's an understatement. I mean, the beginning of hip hop, because I remember reading about the early founding of Def Jam.
sentences.zh: 心想：好吧，Rick在这个人生阶段多大？

sentences.en: And then I was I always like when I'm reading books, I like write out the year that I'm in and then I look up what year that person was born.
sentences.zh: 让我印象深刻的是，读你的书时，我刚读完Jay-Z的《Decoded》。

sentences.en: It's like, OK, how old is Rick at this point that's happening in his life?
sentences.zh: Jay-Z在Def Jam创立十年后，谈论的是他接触嘻哈的早期阶段，那比你接触嘻哈晚了十年。

sentences.en: And what was what I remarkable was like when I was reading your book, I had read this is after I read Jay-Z's book Decoded.
sentences.zh: 他说了一句很棒的话。

sentences.en: And Jay-Z, 10 years after you're starting Def Jam is talking about the early days of hip hop when he got into it, which is a decade after you got into it.
sentences.zh: 他说：我绝对没法告诉你我能靠说唱发财。

sentences.en: And he says something that's really great.
sentences.zh: 我只是知道嘻哈在消失之前会变得更大。

sentences.en: He's just like, I definitely couldn't tell you that I could get rich from rap.
sentences.zh: 那比你所处的阶段晚了十年。

sentences.en: I just knew that hip hop was going to get a lot bigger before it goes away.
sentences.zh: 而在我当时所处的阶段，我绝不会说它会变大。

sentences.en: That's a decade later than where you're at.
sentences.zh: 我当时处于那种阶段：我要做这个，而那几个喜欢它的人都会喜欢它。

sentences.en: And where I was, I would not have said it'll ever get big.
sentences.zh: 仅此而已。没有上升空间。根本没想过会有其他人喜欢它。

sentences.en: I was in the stage where I'm going to make this and the few people who like this will all like it.
sentences.zh: 它就是这么地下。LL Cool J是你制作的第一个人吗？

sentences.en: And that's it. There was no upside. There was no thinking anybody else is going to like this.
sentences.zh: 我制作的第一张嘻哈唱片是T La Rock的《It's Yours》。

sentences.en: That's how underground it was. Is LL Coolidge the first person you produced?
sentences.zh: 好的。那是一张单曲。就是那张在18个月里卖了10万张的唱片。

sentences.en: The first hip hop record I produced was T La Rock, It's Yours.
sentences.zh: 然后LL的第一张唱片是那之后的下一张。

sentences.en: Okay. It was one single. That's the one that sold 100,000 copies in 18 months.
sentences.zh: 但哪一张是在封套上写了“Produced by Rick Rubin”并印上你宿舍地址的？

sentences.en: And then LL's first record was the first record after that.
sentences.zh: 是的。我想可能每一张都有宿舍地址，因为我当时就住在那儿。至于“Produced by”，我可能是在LL的唱片上第一次这么写的。

sentences.en: But which is the one where you put Reduced by Rick Rubin on a sleeve and then your dorm room address?
sentences.zh: 这就是让我着迷的地方。

sentences.en: Yeah. I think all of them probably had the dorm room address because that's where I lived. and reduced by, I probably said it for the first time on LL's record.
sentences.zh: 就像“少即是多”，但要得到“少”，你必须做更多。剥离掉一切，几乎像是一种对极简主义和永恒理念的宗教式虔诚。

sentences.en: This is the thing that I'm fascinated with.
sentences.zh: 你当时才18、19岁，就把这个写在他的唱片上了。

sentences.en: It's like less is more, but to get less, you have to do more. stripping away of everything that's just like almost like religious devotion to simplicity and like timeless ideas.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我思考过“Produced by”这个概念，我以为这个词的意思是“建立”。

sentences.en: You were 19, 18 years old when you put that on his record.
sentences.zh: 我把制作看作是构建。但实际上我做的是拆解和精简。

sentences.en: Well, I thought about the idea of produced by, and I thought the word meant to build up.
sentences.zh: 我想也许“Reduced by”在这种情况下更准确。

sentences.en: Like I think of production as building. And really what I was doing was taking apart and reducing.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样发生的。所以他带给你一首歌，东西太多了？

sentences.en: I thought maybe reducing would be reduced by is more accurate in this case.
sentences.zh: 你是在删减什么？在那些日子里，那还不是“歌”。

sentences.en: And that's, that's how it happened. So he brings you a song and there's just too much.
sentences.zh: 他只有笔记本，上面写满了歌词，而且不是按歌曲顺序排列的。

sentences.en: Like, what are you taking away? In those days, it weren't, he didn't, it weren't songs.
sentences.zh: 那只是押韵。我们会一起看所有的歌词，问：这里面有没有什么可以作为歌曲的基础？比如我需要一个节拍，可能是一个可以重复的短语，最终成为副歌。很多Def Jam之前的嘻哈唱片，就是某人开始说唱，然后说唱几分钟，然后结束。

sentences.en: It would be, um, he would just have notebooks of lyrics and they weren't in song order.
sentences.zh: 那不像一首歌。更像是一段独白。

sentences.en: It was just rhymes. and we would look at all the lyrics together and say is there something here that could be the basis of a song like i need a beat for example that could be a repeated phrase that ends up being a hook and and the reason like many of the hip-hop records before the def jam records were somebody would start rapping and then they would rap for a few minutes and then they would finish rapping.
sentences.zh: 几乎像是对着节拍念白？差不多，但还是说唱风格，只是没有歌曲结构。

sentences.en: It wasn't like a song. It was more like a monologue.
sentences.zh: 就像牙买加的Toasting（念白）。但我是在披头士的音乐中长大的，我热爱披头士，我对音乐的理解基于披头士。

sentences.en: Almost like spoken word to a beat? Kind of, but it was still in a rap style, but it wasn't in a song structure.
sentences.zh: 而披头士是史上最伟大的词曲作者。

sentences.en: It was like Jamaican toasting. But the fact that I grew up on the Beatles and loved the Beatles and my understanding of music is based on the Beatles.
sentences.zh: 他们的歌曲结构非常有条理且紧凑。

sentences.en: And the Beatles were the greatest songwriters ever.
sentences.zh: 所以基于我对披头士的了解，我把它应用到了说唱音乐上，让它结构化得更像一首披头士的歌，而不是一段独白或牙买加的Toasting唱片。

sentences.en: And the structure their songs are really organized and tight.
sentences.zh: 好的，从你和LL Cool J合作到现在，已经过去四十年了。

sentences.en: So based on what I knew about from listening to the Beatles, I applied that to rap music so that it would be structured more like a Beatles song instead of like a monologue or a Jamaican toasting record.
sentences.zh: 如果你今天和一位艺术家合作，你所做的事情与四十年前和LL合作时相比，有多大的相似或不同？可能差别不大，其实挺相似的。这取决于艺术家，因为LL是个人说唱歌手，他没有乐队，也不制作音乐，我负责制作伴奏，我的版本是非常精简、极简的东西。但现在我有时会和有大音效的乐队合作，有很多乐手，我在寻找这些艺术家各自的本质，而本质往往是精简的，但那是精简到他们原本的样子。我刚和The Strokes完成了一张新专辑，他们是一个五人乐队，所以听起来就像一个五人乐队，不会听起来比那更少。

sentences.en: Okay, so there is four decades separating when you're working with LL, Cool J, and today.
sentences.zh: 听起来就是他们本来的样子。你有一个“无情编辑”的理念。

sentences.en: How similar or different from what, like if you're working with an artist today how different is what you're doing with that artist today compared to what you did with LL four decades ago probably not so different it's it's probably pretty similar just it it depends on the artist like because LL was a solo rap artist and he didn't have a band or make music I was responsible for making the the tracks and my version of that was a very stripped down minimal thing but now i get to work with bands sometimes that have a big sound and there are a lot of players and i'm looking for the essence of each of these artists and the essence tends to be stripped down but it's stripped down to what they are just finished a new album with the strokes and they're a band of five people so it sounds like a band of five people doesn't sound less than that.
sentences.zh: 我在播客里听你提过几次。

sentences.en: It sounds like what they are. You have this idea of ruthless edit.
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下那是什么吗？

sentences.en: I've heard you talk about it a few times on podcasts.
sentences.zh: 有时为了整体作品，移除你真正喜欢的部分也是过程的一部分。

sentences.en: Can you explain what that is?
sentences.zh: 如果你有100%，你知道最后想要保留70%，也就是多了30%。

sentences.en: Sometimes for the sake of the whole work, removing things about it that you really love is part of the process.
sentences.zh: 与其把那30%一点点削减到70%，我会说，把它减到40%。

sentences.en: And And instead of if you have 100% and you know at the end you want to have 70% of what you have, like you have 30% too much.
sentences.zh: 强迫自己减到40%。然后再加回达到70%所必需的东西。

sentences.en: Instead of whittling down that 30 to get to the 70, I would say reduce it to 40%, let's say.
sentences.zh: 这是一种不同的运作方式。在“无情编辑”之后，你会对作品有更好的理解，因为你会发现，特别是在团队中，因为在团队里，每个人都要投票。

sentences.en: Force yourself to get to 40%. And then add back. what's needed to get to the 70.
sentences.zh: 比如Red Hot Chili Peppers，我们录一张专辑可能会录40到50首歌，然后我们所有人投票选出A、B或C。如果大家都选它作为专辑里的一首歌，那它就在；如果分歧很大，可能就不会。这是一个民主的过程，直到我们选出大家一致认为是我们能做出的最好的东西。这就是无情编辑的过程，你只是在寻找你认为能成就伟大的本质。所以在那情况下，你们录了50首歌。

sentences.en: And it works in a different way. You have a better understanding of the work after the Ruthless Edit, because you find out, especially with a group, because in a group, everybody votes.
sentences.zh: 而你说专辑想要10到12首。

sentences.en: So with the Red Hot Chili Peppers, we'll record, for an album, we might record 40 or 50 songs, and then all of us vote on A, B, or C. and then if everyone picks it as an a song that's going to be on the album if it's really divided it might not be you know it'll be it'll be a democratic process until we get down to like what is everyone together think is the best thing that we can make that's a ruthless editing process and you're just looking for the essence of what you think it could be great so like in that case you're recording, let's say, 50 songs.
sentences.zh: 那，有没有可能，有三首是我们无法割舍的？

sentences.en: And you say the album wants to have 10 or 12.
sentences.zh: 这是思考过程吗？这有助于达到那种“哪些是你无法割舍的”地步，无论有多少首，然后从那里开始构建，向外扩展。

sentences.en: Well, what about, there's like, there might be three that we can't live without.
sentences.zh: 除了音乐，你还有什么兴趣？

sentences.en: Is that the thought process? It helps to get to that point of what are the ones you can't live without, however few it is, and build from there, build out from there.
sentences.zh: 比如，你对建筑感兴趣吗？有没有人在不同领域，你依然保持着热情，并且看到他们使用了和你相似的理念？

sentences.en: What other interests do you have outside of music?
sentences.zh: 在每个领域，都有人创造出美丽的事物。

sentences.en: Like, are you into like architecture? Like, is there anybody, the reason I ask you that is like, is there anybody else in different domains that you still have a passion for, that you see that use similar ideas that you do?
sentences.zh: 我喜欢那些创造美丽事物的人。

sentences.en: In every domain, there are people who make beautiful things.
sentences.zh: 但你能看到他们的思考过程吗？

sentences.en: I like people who make beautiful things.
sentences.zh: 你发现他们的思考过程和他们对工作的推动力之间有相似之处吗？

sentences.en: But are you seeing their thought process?
sentences.zh: 都是一样的。我觉得我所做的大部分事情其实与音乐无关。

sentences.en: Do you find similarities between their thought process and their push to work?
sentences.zh: 我恰好在音乐领域工作，但这与音乐本身无关。

sentences.en: It's all the same. I think most of what I do is not really about music.
sentences.zh: 这说得通吗？说得通，但能多说一点吗？

sentences.en: I happen to work in music, but it's not about the music.
sentences.zh: 你在Shangri-La，走过那个空间，你会觉得它和你去过的其他地方感觉不一样。是的，它和我制作的唱片、我参与的项目、我喜欢的东西、我购买的物品有着相同的审美，所以这一切都符合一种世界观。是的，我也这么觉得，因为我们在录音前聊过播客，我觉得我们都有同样的痴迷。我的第一个播客做了十多年，起初只是我读那些创业者的传记，但随着时间推移，我意识到这种人格类型——艺术家、企业家、电影制作人、音乐人——我做过所有这些人的播客，我看不出他们之间有什么区别。

sentences.en: Does that make sense? It does, but say more about this.
sentences.zh: 是的，是一样的。都是创造性的精神。我想，我有几个自私的问题想问你，因为有些人对我的人生影响巨大。我告诉过你，我从小听嘻哈长大，直到今天我听的还是嘻哈。我现在听播客比听音乐多，但它确实为我内心的一种感觉赋予了声音，甚至可能是在潜意识里。Eminem是第一个让我觉得——我听了他的第一张专辑，心想：这就是我的感受。我虽然不是在密歇根的拖车公园长大的，但我完全明白你在某些家庭琐事或成长过程中所说的那种感觉。我听你说过一次，我简直痴迷了，我想花时间和他在一起，希望能让他录一期播客。我知道这很难，但特别是对你这样在近半个世纪里与最顶尖的人合作过的人来说，你说他可能是你合作过最痴迷的艺术家。

sentences.en: You're at Shangri-La and you walk through the space and you see it doesn't feel like other places you've been. yeah it it has the same aesthetic as the records i make or the things that i work on the things that i like things that i buy you know the objects i buy would have the same aesthetic so it's all fitting into a i'd say worldview yeah i feel this way too because like i mean we talked right before we started recording about you know podcasting i think we're both i have the same obsession with it and i've had my first podcast for over a decade and it started out just me reading biographies of people that build businesses but over time i realized like this same personality type it's like the artist the entrepreneur the filmmaker the musician i've done podcasts on all these kind of people and i'm like i don't see any distinction between them yeah it's the same yeah it's all the creative spirit i want to like they have a bunch of like selfish things i told you i want to talk to you about because there's just some people that have made massive impacts on my life i told you like i grew up listening to hip-hop it's all i listen to this day i listen to more podcasts i'm listening to music now but like it really gave like a put a voice like a words to a feeling i had even maybe in my subconscious eminem was the first one that like i was i heard his first album i was like this is how i feel i didn't grow up in a trailer park in michigan but i know exactly what you're talking about with certain things with your family or certain things of like just becoming you know coming of age i heard you say one time i'm like obsessed with i want to spend time with him and hopefully get him record a podcast i know it's be very difficult but especially for you who've worked with you know the best the best of the best people over almost half a century and for you to say that he might be the most obsessive artist yeah they've ever worked for it was like i literally screenshotted that and saved it on my phone i look at it all the time why did you say that can you just tell me about what it's like working with them it feels like his entire life is centered around writing words he's totally preoccupied with that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我当时真的截了屏保存在手机里，我经常看。你为什么那么说？你能告诉我跟他工作是什么感觉吗？感觉他的一生都围绕着写词，他完全沉浸在其中。

sentences.en: So he always has a notebook. He's always making little notes.
sentences.zh: 所以他总是带着笔记本。他总是记些小笔记。

sentences.en: He writes tiny and tiny letters and he's always making notes.
sentences.zh: 他写字非常小，总是记笔记。

sentences.en: And at one point I asked him, because he's got notebooks and notebooks and notebooks, and I said, are you working on a new song?
sentences.zh: 有一次我问他，因为他有无数本笔记本，我问：你在写新歌吗？

sentences.en: He's like, no, I'm just like...
sentences.zh: 他说：不，我只是……

sentences.en: Keeping active, keeping active in the skill set.
sentences.zh: 保持活跃，保持技能的活跃度。

sentences.en: And I said, are you going to put those in a song?
sentences.zh: 我说：你会把这些写进歌里吗？

sentences.en: He's probably said 90% of it will never be in a song.
sentences.zh: 他大概说90%永远不会进歌里。

sentences.en: He's just writing, just writing. And that's what he does.
sentences.zh: 他只是在写，一直在写。这就是他做的事。

sentences.en: He writes. Does he apply that to like other elements of making a song though?
sentences.zh: 他写歌。但他会把这种劲头用到制作歌曲的其他环节吗？

sentences.en: Just not just writing? Because he does a lot of his own production, right?
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是写歌？因为他自己也做很多制作工作，对吧？

sentences.en: He does. And I would say the same type of obsessive.
sentences.zh: 确实。而且我觉得他那种执着劲儿是一样的。

sentences.en: It's what makes him great. He's obsessed.
sentences.zh: 这就是他伟大的原因。他是个偏执狂。

sentences.en: Have you come across anybody that you consider great that's not obsessed?
sentences.zh: 你有没有遇到过你认为伟大但并不执着的人？

sentences.en: I'm sure there are. I have to think about it.
sentences.zh: 肯定有吧。我得好好想想。

sentences.en: But that's not the only way to do it. For some people, it happens in a more natural way.
sentences.zh: 但那并不是唯一的成功之道。对有些人来说，一切发生得更自然。

sentences.en: And for some people, it's more of a... Work ethic is always a part of it.
sentences.zh: 而对有些人来说，更多是……职业素养始终是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: But for some people, work ethic is the reason they are who they are.
sentences.zh: 但对有些人而言，职业素养正是他们之所以成为他们的原因。

sentences.en: And there are other people who are just incredibly talented and have enough work ethic to get over the finish line.
sentences.zh: 还有些人天赋异禀，只要有足够的职业素养就能冲过终点线。

sentences.en: What do you think it's for you? I don't like to quit.
sentences.zh: 你觉得你属于哪种？我不喜欢半途而废。

sentences.en: I like to see things through. When I start something, I like to see what it can be.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢善始善终。当我开始做一件事，我喜欢看看它最终能变成什么样。

sentences.en: From the outside, because you have this whole very relaxed zen vibe.
sentences.zh: 从外表看，你总是给人一种非常放松、禅意十足的感觉。

sentences.en: Yeah. I swear I think underneath is like a workaholic.
sentences.zh: 是啊。但我发誓，我内心其实是个工作狂。

sentences.en: Oh, for sure. Okay. For sure. I'm a lazy workaholic.
sentences.zh: 哦，那肯定的。好吧。确实。我是个懒散的工作狂。

sentences.en: Lazy workaholic. You got to say more about that.
sentences.zh: 懒散的工作狂。你得再多解释一下。

sentences.en: That's what it is. Because it doesn't feel like work?
sentences.zh: 就是这样。因为这感觉不像是在工作？

sentences.en: Explain. No, no, no. I have to force myself to do it, but I do force myself.
sentences.zh: 解释一下。不，不，不。我得强迫自己去做，但我确实在强迫自己。

sentences.en: My demeanor would be to do nothing. Rick, I don't believe that.
sentences.zh: 我的本性其实是想什么都不做。Rick，我不信。

sentences.en: It's true. No, you love this too much, though.
sentences.zh: 是真的。不过，你太热爱这件事了。

sentences.en: What do you mean? So I love the beautiful thing, and it takes a lot of work to get to the beautiful thing.
sentences.zh: 什么意思？我是热爱美好的事物，而要达到那种美好，需要付出大量的工作。

sentences.en: You like the end result? Yeah, I like to get there.
sentences.zh: 你喜欢的是最终结果？是的，我喜欢达成那个结果。

sentences.en: I like to get to the point where it's like, okay, press the send button and share it with the world.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢达到那种状态，就是那种，好吧，按下发送键，与世界分享它。

sentences.en: That's a great feeling. Like, I like it enough for you to get to hear it.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉很棒。就像，我喜欢它到足以让你听到它的程度。

sentences.en: Okay. But all of the work up until then, it's like, oh, my God, I have to go to the studio today.
sentences.zh: 好吧。但在那之前所有的工作，就像是，天哪，我今天还得去录音室。

sentences.en: That's surprising to me. Yeah. It's such a beautiful day.
sentences.zh: 这让我很惊讶。是啊。明明是这么美好的一天。

sentences.en: Wouldn't it be nice to just go out and have lunch with friends?
sentences.zh: 难道出去和朋友吃顿午饭不是更好吗？

sentences.en: But my whole life has been, you know, most of my life was in the first 25 years, This was in a dark room for 16 hours a day, seven days a week in New York City working on music.
sentences.zh: 但我的一生，你知道，我生命中大部分时间，前25年，都是在纽约一个昏暗的房间里，每天16小时，每周7天，埋头做音乐。

sentences.en: Now, you'd rather be out here barefoot, butt naked in the sun, I think.
sentences.zh: 现在，我觉得你更愿意光着脚、光着屁股在阳光下待着。

sentences.en: Now. But not then. Not then. Okay. But I like being outside.
sentences.zh: 现在是。但那时不是。那时不是。好吧。但我确实喜欢待在户外。

sentences.en: I like having fun with friends. I like hanging out with my family.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢和朋友玩得开心。我喜欢和家人待在一起。

sentences.en: Do you like making podcasts more than music now?
sentences.zh: 你现在比做音乐更喜欢做播客吗？

sentences.en: I don't know if it's I like it more. I like the people I get to meet, and I'm interested in learning about people.
sentences.zh: 我不知道是不是更喜欢。我喜欢我能见到的人，而且我对了解人很感兴趣。

sentences.en: I like learning how people think, their vision to make something, how they follow through to make it, and learning the rollercoaster ride, that journey of building things, how it worked, where it didn't work, what ideas they thought may have worked that didn't, when they were surprised in the process.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢了解人们的思维方式，他们创造某样东西的愿景，他们如何坚持到底去完成它，以及了解那个过山车般的旅程，那种创造事物的过程，它是如何运作的，哪里行不通，他们认为哪些想法可行但实际上不行，他们在过程中何时感到惊喜。

sentences.en: It's all interesting to me. I want to like pull on this for a little bit if you don't mind so I heard Billie Eilish's brother who I think they have a close collaboration with so he was describing the difference between him and Billie he said that he enjoyed the process of making music she enjoyed having made the music so are you more like Billie in that case like you like that it's done?
sentences.zh: 这一切对我来说都很有趣。如果你不介意的话，我想深入探讨一下，我听说Billie Eilish的哥哥，我想他们合作很紧密，他描述过他和Billie的区别，他说他享受制作音乐的过程，而她享受的是音乐制作完成后的成果，那么在这种情况下，你更像Billie吗？你喜欢它完成的那一刻？

sentences.en: I think so I'll say I like the moment of revelation.
sentences.zh: 我想是的，我会说我喜欢那种顿悟的时刻。

sentences.en: So we're working on something. It's just okay.
sentences.zh: 所以我们正在做某件事。它只是还可以。

sentences.en: It's boring.
sentences.zh: 很无聊。

sentences.en: I'd probably rather not be there. That's how it feels.
sentences.zh: 我可能宁愿不在那儿。感觉就是这样。

sentences.en: But then something happens and it's like magic, like something appears.
sentences.zh: 但突然发生了什么，就像魔法一样，有什么东西显现出来了。

sentences.en: It doesn't, it's not like we made it. It's like something comes up in the process.
sentences.zh: 不是说我们制造了它。而是过程中有什么东西浮现了出来。

sentences.en: It's conjured in the process. That's like a miracle.
sentences.zh: 它是过程中被召唤出来的。那就像个奇迹。

sentences.en: And that's the thing that's addictive. That feeling when it's like, it's not good.
sentences.zh: 而那正是让人上瘾的东西。那种感觉，当它还不够好时。

sentences.en: It's not good. It's not good. It's not good. we try this we try this this doesn't work this doesn't work this doesn't work and it could be a mistake the machine could not work we can hear something out of the machine broke but what you but what we're listening to is really cool all of a sudden that's the feeling that that moment of discovery where it goes from nothing to something really good and then the whole rest of the process after that is protecting that because it's super delicate when it happens it's like this miracle happened and this magic thing happened and now we have to protect it through the rest of the process to not ruin it when it comes together let's say a band is playing and doing take after take after take when it's really good we all kind of look at each other like as they're playing it's like it's scary because you don't want it to end like you don't want it to stop because we know if it stops we can't control it we can't do it again it's not like that it's this moment in time where something magical happens so we spend a lot of time waiting for those but i can't say that's fun it's not fun it's it's just like takes a lot of You have to force yourself to do it.
sentences.zh: 它不够好。它不够好。它不够好。我们尝试这个，尝试那个，这个不行，那个不行，这个也不行，甚至可能是一个错误，机器可能出了故障，我们可能听到了机器坏掉的声音，但我们听到的东西突然变得非常酷，那就是那种感觉，那种从无到有、发现真正好东西的时刻，然后剩下的整个过程就是保护它，因为它在发生时非常脆弱，就像奇迹发生了，魔法发生了，现在我们必须在剩下的过程中保护它，不要在它成型时毁了它。比方说一个乐队正在演奏，一遍又一遍地录音，当它真的很好时，我们都会看着对方，就像他们演奏时那样，这很吓人，因为你不想让它结束，因为你不想让它停止，因为我们知道如果它停止了，我们就无法控制它，我们无法再做一次，它不是那样的，它是时间里的一个瞬间，某种神奇的事情发生了，所以我们花了很多时间等待这些时刻，但我不能说那很有趣，那并不有趣，它只是需要付出很多，你必须强迫自己去做。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Have you ever just like gave up in that moment, just walked away for a little bit?
sentences.zh: 你有没有在那一刻放弃过，直接走开了一会儿？

sentences.en: Mm-hmm. Okay, so you do have this like really— Yeah, a little work ethic.
sentences.zh: 嗯。好吧，所以你确实有这种……是的，有一点职业素养。

sentences.en: You have work ethic and discipline. Yeah.
sentences.zh: 你有职业素养和纪律性。是的。

sentences.en: Okay. But it would still be if you could— It's frustrating and boring and takes a great deal of patience.
sentences.zh: 好吧。但如果可以的话，它仍然会是……这很令人沮丧，很无聊，需要极大的耐心。

sentences.en: It's like waiting for paint to dry, just waiting, waiting, waiting, and trying different things and nothing works. until something either works or something happens and it just comes together.
sentences.zh: 就像等待油漆干透，只是等待，等待，等待，尝试不同的东西，什么都不管用。直到要么什么东西管用了，要么发生了什么，它就自然而然地整合在一起了。

sentences.en: And I can't tell you why. Explain what people do to kill these special moments, though.
sentences.zh: 我没法告诉你为什么。不过，解释一下人们做些什么会毁掉这些特殊时刻吧。

sentences.en: You kept saying, like, we have to protect this.
sentences.zh: 你一直说，我们必须保护它。

sentences.en: Once you're aware of it, it's harder to protect.
sentences.zh: 一旦你意识到它，就更难保护了。

sentences.en: Like, in the process of it happening, if you realize this is it, it's like, what is it, engulf the yips.
sentences.zh: 就像，在它发生的过程中，如果你意识到这就是那个时刻，就像，怎么说呢，陷入了“易普症”（yips）。

sentences.en: You know, like when you're playing golf, if you start thinking about it instead of just being in it, you can't do it anymore.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像打高尔夫球时，如果你开始思考它，而不是沉浸其中，你就再也打不好了。

sentences.en: So it's almost like you have to get out of yourself to allow it to happen.
sentences.zh: 所以几乎就像你必须跳出自我，才能让它发生。

sentences.en: Maybe not me, but for the artist. The artist has to get to this place where it's like they don't even know they're doing it.
sentences.zh: 也许不是我，但对于艺术家来说。艺术家必须达到那种状态，就是他们甚至不知道自己在做这件事。

sentences.en: It just happens. It's not a performance.
sentences.zh: 它自然就发生了。这不是表演。

sentences.en: It's something else. It's just like a real moment happens and it's thrilling.
sentences.zh: 它是别的东西。就是一个真实的瞬间发生了，这让人激动。

sentences.en: I think you're speaking to my soul right now because there's something I heard Steph Curry talk about one time where they're like, what do you think of when you're taking a shot?
sentences.zh: 我觉得你现在说到了我的心坎里，因为我曾经听Steph Curry谈过一件事，当时有人问他，你在投篮时在想什么？

sentences.en: And he goes, absolutely nothing. Exactly.
sentences.zh: 他说，什么都不想。没错。

sentences.en: And so like when I read books for a living, essentially, before I started this, and you know, people, I've had authors reach out to me after I did their book and they're like, how did you get to the essence of it?
sentences.zh: 所以，当我以读书为生时，基本上，在我开始做这个之前，你知道，人们，有些作者在我读完他们的书后联系我，他们问，你是怎么抓住它的精髓的？

sentences.en: Like, what were you thinking? What are you thinking of when you're doing this?
sentences.zh: 就像，你在想什么？你在做这件事时在想什么？

sentences.en: And I was like, nothing. I just read. And if something sticks, jumps out to me, I don't think at all.
sentences.zh: 我说，什么都没想。我只是读。如果有什么东西触动了我，跳了出来，我根本不去思考。

sentences.en: I just underline it. And then I'll go back through it when I reread the highlight.
sentences.zh: 我只是把它划线。然后当我重读高亮部分时，我会再看一遍。

sentences.en: If it's still interesting, it was interesting the first time.
sentences.zh: 如果它依然有趣，那它第一次就是有趣的。

sentences.en: Now it's interesting the second time. It's probably interesting.
sentences.zh: 现在第二次看它依然有趣。那它可能确实有趣。

sentences.en: There's 10 million me's out there. I'm not unique.
sentences.zh: 外面有千万个我。我并不独特。

sentences.en: Same. And there's no way I read this line twice.
sentences.zh: 我也是。而且我不可能把这一行读两遍。

sentences.en: And if I read it on a podcast that somebody else is not going to think of it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 如果我在播客上读了它，别人可能不会觉得它有趣。

sentences.en: He's like, if I overthink it or if I think of, oh, this person might hear it or this kind of this many people will hear it.
sentences.zh: 他就像是，如果我过度思考，或者如果我想到，哦，这个人可能会听到，或者会有这么多人听到。

sentences.en: It's in the way. Nothing. I'm thinking of nothing.
sentences.zh: 那就会碍事。什么都没有。我什么都没想。

sentences.en: Yes. That's really interesting. So let me ask you this, though.
sentences.zh: 是的。这真的很有趣。不过让我问你这个。

sentences.en: So you're fucking Rick Rubin. You can do whatever you want.
sentences.zh: 你可是Rick Rubin。你可以做任何你想做的事。

sentences.en: Why are you choosing to spend so much time podcasting then?
sentences.zh: 那你为什么选择花这么多时间做播客呢？

sentences.en: I like meeting the people. And even before the podcast started, I would still, if someone was interesting to me, I would reach out to them, want to spend time with them, hang out with them, and just learn from them, really.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢结识这些人。即使在播客开始之前，如果有人让我感兴趣，我还是会联系他们，想和他们共度时光，和他们待在一起，真正地向他们学习。

sentences.en: I can remember the one where it became obvious to do the podcast was Dana White.
sentences.zh: 我记得很清楚，做播客变得显而易见的那一次是Dana White。

sentences.en: Someone introduced me to Dana White. I'm recording with him next week.
sentences.zh: 有人把我介绍给了Dana White。我下周要和他录音。

sentences.en: Great. He's great. He's incredible. And I said, he actually reached out to me.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。他很棒。他不可思议。我说，其实是他主动联系我的。

sentences.en: He's like, anytime you want to meet, I'm down.
sentences.zh: 他说，任何时候你想见面，我都奉陪。

sentences.en: He's like, great, let's do it. We met. We sat at my house.
sentences.zh: 他说，太棒了，我们就这么干。我们见面了，坐在我家。

sentences.en: We sat outside. We talked for about three hours.
sentences.zh: 我们坐在外面，聊了大概三个小时。

sentences.en: And at some point in the conversation, I said, do you mind if I record this?
sentences.zh: 聊到某个点时，我问他，介意我录下来吗？

sentences.en: Because I feel like I'm not going to remember what we're saying. and I'm really liking this story.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得我记不住我们聊的内容，而且我真的很喜欢这个故事。

sentences.en: And that was sort of a breakthrough of like, this is kind of what doing a podcast is like.
sentences.zh: 那算是一个突破点，让我意识到，做播客大概就是这种感觉。

sentences.en: I already do this in my life. I don't record them, but I meet the people that make things that are interesting to me and I spend time with them and I listen to what they do and I ask a lot of questions because I'm curious.
sentences.zh: 我生活中本来就在做这种事。我虽然不录音，但我会去见那些做出有趣东西的人，花时间陪他们，听他们怎么做，并问很多问题，因为我很好奇。

sentences.en: So it really is an outgrowth of my normal life.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是我正常生活的延伸。

sentences.en: So I like doing that. We were talking before we started recording, like I may be the person that's most obsessed with podcasting in the world.
sentences.zh: 所以我喜欢这样做。我们在录音前聊天时提到，我可能是世界上最痴迷播客的人。

sentences.en: I listened to thousands of episodes. I was listening to your podcast, Broken Record, back in the day.
sentences.zh: 我听过几千集节目。我以前就听过你的播客《Broken Record》。

sentences.en: I was like, this is incredible. And you were heavily into interviewing musicians back then.
sentences.zh: 当时我就觉得，这太不可思议了。你那时候非常热衷于采访音乐人。

sentences.en: That was the format of that show, was just talking to musicians.
sentences.zh: 那个节目的形式就是和音乐人聊天。

sentences.en: And then Tetragrammaton, you took, in my opinion, to another level.
sentences.zh: 然后到了《Tetragrammaton》，在我看来，你把它提升到了另一个高度。

sentences.en: And you're talking to all kinds of incredible people.
sentences.zh: 你采访了各种各样了不起的人。

sentences.en: I listened to, I just had a conversation with Toby Luque, founder of Shopify.
sentences.zh: 我刚听了你和 Shopify 创始人 Toby Luque 的对话。

sentences.en: Yeah, amazing. I used one of your episodes to prep because he's such a unique mind.
sentences.zh: 没错，太棒了。我用你那一集来做准备，因为他的思维太独特了。

sentences.en: One of the most interesting conversations I had. but I was I analyzed people like you know there's a handful of podcasts are really great there's a couple million in the directory only a handful are really great yours is really great and I'm like why the hell how it's unfair this guy is like gifted at music and now he's gifted podcasting why is this the case and what I came up with and I started analyzing and thinking about what you do in your day job what you've done for over four decades and I was like he's a professional listener That's true.
sentences.zh: 那是我进行过最有趣的对话之一。但我分析过像你这样的人，你知道，播客里有几百万个节目，但真正出色的只有寥寥几个，你的节目真的很棒。我就在想，凭什么？这不公平，这家伙在音乐上天赋异禀，现在做播客也这么有天赋，这是为什么？我分析并思考了你几十年来一直从事的主业，我意识到，你是一个专业的倾听者。确实如此。

sentences.en: I don't, he's listening to the guest. He is in the moment with the guest.
sentences.zh: 我不，他是在倾听嘉宾。他完全沉浸在与嘉宾的当下。

sentences.en: Yes. And it's like, that is why one of the reasons why, obviously you have a lot of interesting things to say, but one of the reasons, in my opinion, that you're so great at podcasting.
sentences.zh: 是的。这就是原因之一，显然你有很多有趣的观点，但在我看来，你之所以在播客方面如此出色，原因之一就在于此。

sentences.en: Well, I think in real life, people like to talk and they don't like to listen.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为在现实生活中，人们喜欢说，却不喜欢听。

sentences.en: And often in a conversation, you'll be with someone and they'll be saying something and you'll be thinking about, okay, this is what I'm going to say in response to that.
sentences.zh: 通常在对话中，你和某人在一起，当对方在说话时，你脑子里想的却是：好吧，等会儿我该怎么回应他。

sentences.en: You're not really present back and forth.
sentences.zh: 你并没有真正投入到互动中。

sentences.en: That's what it is. Like two people waiting for their turn to say what they think.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。就像两个人都在等轮到自己发表观点一样。

sentences.en: And this is different. And it really, I think it came from listening to music because I listen to music in a very deep way.
sentences.zh: 而这（我的方式）不同。我认为这源于我听音乐的习惯，因为我听音乐的方式非常深入。

sentences.en: I close my eyes. I really pay attention.
sentences.zh: 我会闭上眼睛，真正地去专注。

sentences.en: It's not wallpaper. It's like I go into the music.
sentences.zh: 那不是背景噪音。我像是走进了音乐里。

sentences.en: In some ways, I think my relationship with music allowed me to never drink or take drugs because listening to music for me is totally a psychedelic experience.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我认为我和音乐的关系让我从不喝酒或吸毒，因为对我来说，听音乐本身就是一种迷幻体验。

sentences.en: I can feel the music. and I can be transported by the music.
sentences.zh: 我能感受到音乐，也能被音乐带走。

sentences.en: Not all music, but good music. So I close my eyes, I feel it, and then at the end of it I open my eyes and I'm surprised where I am because I've been gone when I'm listening.
sentences.zh: 不是所有音乐，但好的音乐可以。所以我闭上眼睛，感受它，当音乐结束时，我睁开眼，会惊讶于自己身在何处，因为我刚才已经神游物外了。

sentences.en: So I listen deeply and I wanna know, I really wanna understand things.
sentences.zh: 所以我倾听得很深，我想知道，我真的想理解事物。

sentences.en: So I'm comfortable asking questions and I really listen to what someone's saying.
sentences.zh: 所以我很乐意提问，并且我真的在听对方在说什么。

sentences.en: And if someone says something I don't understand, And I'll ask a question to clarify so that I can understand it.
sentences.zh: 如果对方说了我不理解的话，我会问问题来澄清，以便我能理解。

sentences.en: I also don't have any judgment. I don't think that I have a way that like my way is the right way.
sentences.zh: 我也没有任何评判。我不认为我有一种所谓的“正确方式”。

sentences.en: And I'm not comparing what's being said to me about what I think.
sentences.zh: 我不会拿对方说的话和我自己的想法做比较。

sentences.en: What I think is not part of it. I'm just, I just want to truly understand what's being shared with me.
sentences.zh: 我的想法并不重要。我只是，我只是想真正理解对方在分享什么。

sentences.en: And if someone says something that's very different than what I believe, I want to know more.
sentences.zh: 如果有人说的和我相信的非常不同，我想了解更多。

sentences.en: It's like, how did he get to that? Why do you think that?
sentences.zh: 就像是，他是怎么得出这个结论的？你为什么会这么想？

sentences.en: Because maybe I'll learn something. Maybe I have it wrong, you know, like that.
sentences.zh: 因为也许我能学到点什么。也许是我错了，你知道，就是这样。

sentences.en: I don't know anything. I want to know more.
sentences.zh: 我什么都不知道。我想知道更多。

sentences.en: So through talking to people and really listening, you really get to meet people.
sentences.zh: 所以通过与人交谈并真正倾听，你真的能认识这些人。

sentences.en: And as a professional listener, I found some people, it's disarming to talk to someone who really listens because it's so rare.
sentences.zh: 作为一名专业的倾听者，我发现对某些人来说，和一个真正倾听的人交谈会让他们放下防备，因为这太罕见了。

sentences.en: Most people don't listen. when i listen to your podcast i feel you have this combination of like sincere interest yes true in the other human being yes and a desire i think you just said this but the way i think about it is the way i think about you when i listen to your podcast is like a desire not to form an opinion but to understand that's it that's it i just want to understand i want to understand to broaden my scope to see the world i want to see the world through your eyes.
sentences.zh: 大多数人都不听。当我听你的播客时，我感觉到你有一种结合，既有对他人真诚的兴趣，是的，确实如此，还有一种渴望——我想你刚才也说了，但我对你的看法是，当你做播客时，你不是为了形成某种观点，而是为了理解。就是这样，就是这样，我只是想理解。我想通过理解来拓宽我的视野，去观察世界，我想通过你的眼睛看世界。

sentences.en: You know, I want to see the world through someone made something that's beautiful to me.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想通过那些创造了美的人的视角去看世界。

sentences.en: I want to understand how they see the world.
sentences.zh: 我想理解他们是如何看待世界的。

sentences.en: Someone makes a great discovery. I want to know what was the process that allowed that to happen.
sentences.zh: 有人做出了伟大的发现。我想知道是什么过程促成了这一切。

sentences.en: I'm curious. Yeah. It doesn't seem to be an end to your curiosity either.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇。是的，你的好奇心似乎永无止境。

sentences.en: I'm interested. I've always been interested.
sentences.zh: 我很感兴趣。我一直都很有兴趣。

sentences.en: I think of myself as a researcher. I've always, like when the internet came along, anything that I'm interested in, I'll go forever. going deeper and deeper and deeper into a topic just to get any glimpse and to read opposing opinions and go deeper and deeper and deeper and just try and understand.
sentences.zh: 我把自己看作一名研究者。我一直都是这样，比如当互联网出现时，任何我感兴趣的东西，我都会钻研到底。不断深入、深入、再深入地挖掘一个话题，只为了窥见一斑，去阅读对立的观点，不断深入，只是为了尝试去理解。

sentences.en: I'm curious. You think of yourself as a researcher.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇。你把自己看作一名研究者。

sentences.en: Yeah. That's what I do most of the time is research.
sentences.zh: 是的。我大部分时间都在做研究。

sentences.en: Okay. I don't know about this. Tell me about this.
sentences.zh: 好吧。我不了解这个。跟我说说这个。

sentences.en: Well, not a researcher in a professional way, but anything I'm interested in, I want to know everything about it, whatever it is, and even mundane things.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不是那种专业意义上的研究者，但任何我感兴趣的东西，我都想了解关于它的一切，无论是什么，甚至是琐碎的事情。

sentences.en: If I drink coffee, I want to taste a million coffee.
sentences.zh: 如果我喝咖啡，我想尝遍一百万种咖啡。

sentences.en: I want to find the best coffee. I want to read what every person who knows about the best machine says about every machine and then test every machine.
sentences.zh: 我想找到最好的咖啡。我想读懂每一个了解顶级咖啡机的人对每一台机器的评价，然后测试每一台机器。

sentences.en: And it's just a fanatical devotion to finding the best version of whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 这只是一种对寻找极致版本的狂热执着。

sentences.en: Is it all consuming for you when you find these pockets of interest?
sentences.zh: 当你发现这些感兴趣的领域时，你会感到全神贯注吗？

sentences.en: I'd say so. There's no end. I don't get to an end to that process.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。没有尽头。我永远无法走到那个过程的终点。

sentences.en: I admire people that do things for a very long period of time.
sentences.zh: 我很钦佩那些长期坚持做一件事的人。

sentences.en: And you can tell a lot about people by what they admire.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过一个人钦佩什么来了解他。

sentences.en: It's like, I want to do these kinds of podcasts till I die.
sentences.zh: 就像，我想一直做这种播客，直到我死去。

sentences.en: Like, it was like, what's your strategy?
sentences.zh: 就像，有人问：你的策略是什么？

sentences.en: What's successful in five years, in 10 years?
sentences.zh: 五年、十年后什么才算成功？

sentences.en: One, that I'm still doing it. And two, I'm just making things that I'm proud of.
sentences.zh: 第一，我还在做。第二，我只是在做让我感到自豪的事情。

sentences.en: That's it. There's no fucking download number.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。没有什么该死的下载量。

sentences.en: There's no how many ads I sell. It's just like, that's it.
sentences.zh: 没有什么我卖了多少广告。就是这样，仅此而已。

sentences.en: And I'm terrified that one day, you know, I'm going to wake up and be like, I don't want to do this anymore.
sentences.zh: 我很害怕有一天，你知道，我会醒来，然后觉得：我不想再做这个了。

sentences.en: No, but the only reason that would happen. is because something else would take over that you have to do and that would be fine too like when i was when i was nine years old i spent a lot of time practicing magic like card magic in front of a mirror and that was really fun and there's a whole community of musician magicians and i was just a little kid but like grown-up magicians and if you're truly interested magic um there are all these meetings and they get together and talk about stuff and And if you're an outsider, everything's a secret.
sentences.zh: 不，但唯一会发生这种情况的原因，是因为有其他事情占据了你的生活，让你不得不去做，那也没关系。就像我九岁的时候，我花了很多时间在镜子前练习魔术，比如纸牌魔术，那真的很有趣。有一个完整的魔术师群体，我当时只是个小孩子，但那些成年魔术师，如果你真的对魔术感兴趣，嗯，他们有很多聚会，大家聚在一起谈论各种事情。如果你是个外行，一切都是秘密。

sentences.en: But if you're a magician, they love sharing.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是魔术师，他们乐于分享。

sentences.en: So it's a really cool community to be part of.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常酷的群体。

sentences.en: And that was my community from nine until probably 16.
sentences.zh: 那是从我九岁到大概十六岁时的圈子。

sentences.en: Those were the people I hung out with. And that were the people that we shared this interest.
sentences.zh: 那些是我常在一起的人。我们分享着同样的兴趣。

sentences.en: And I just wanted to learn. And then music became more and more popular in my life.
sentences.zh: 我只是想学习。然后音乐在我的生活中变得越来越重要。

sentences.en: And then at some point, it's like, I can't do both.
sentences.zh: 然后到了某个时刻，我觉得：我不能两者兼顾。

sentences.en: They're both, these are both full-time occupations.
sentences.zh: 它们都是全职工作。

sentences.en: And when I say occupations, I don't mean jobs.
sentences.zh: 当我说是工作时，我指的不是职业。

sentences.en: I mean something to occupy my time. I can either devote myself to doing magic or devote myself to doing music.
sentences.zh: 我指的是占据我时间的事情。我要么全身心投入做魔术，要么全身心投入做音乐。

sentences.en: And at some point, music won. But that wasn't a loss.
sentences.zh: 最终，音乐胜出了。但这并不是一种损失。

sentences.en: I didn't lose anything. That's a beautiful way to think of it.
sentences.zh: 我没有失去任何东西。这是一种很美的想法。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's like I let go of the thing that I loved for this other thing that I loved that just took on this new life.
sentences.zh: 是的，就像我放下了我所爱的东西，去拥抱了另一件我所爱的事，而它开启了新的生命。

sentences.en: And I've done music for a long time and I like making other things too.
sentences.zh: 我做音乐已经很久了，我也喜欢做其他事情。

sentences.en: And if my life became about making other things more than making music, that'd be okay.
sentences.zh: 如果我的生活重心从做音乐变成了做其他事情，那也没关系。

sentences.en: It's more about the making that excites me.
sentences.zh: 比起结果，创作的过程更让我兴奋。

sentences.en: This is why I kept asking, do you think you would, like making a podcast, like we can have a conversation.
sentences.zh: 这就是我一直问你的原因，你觉得你会做播客吗？就像我们现在这样聊天一样。

sentences.en: We can be doing your show right now instead of mine.
sentences.zh: 我们现在就可以做你的节目，而不是我的。

sentences.en: And at the end of this hour or two hours, like we have it's done we have something we can do it again tomorrow like the the amount of time from you know creation to output is so much shorter than an album or even a great song true and if you're what you're saying i think you call yourself a lazy workaholic i'm saying lazy alcoholic lazy workaholic like it's almost like this doesn't work this doesn't feel like work to me yeah i feel like you i was a little surprised with the way you described working in music that does feel like work to you.
sentences.zh: 在这一个或两个小时结束时，我们就完成了，我们可以明天再来一次。你知道，从创作到产出的时间比做一张专辑甚至一首好歌要短得多。确实，如果你像你所说的，自称是一个懒惰的工作狂——我是说懒惰的酒鬼，懒惰的工作狂——这感觉几乎不像是在工作。是的，我感觉和你一样，你描述在音乐领域工作的方式让我有点惊讶，那对你来说确实感觉像工作。

sentences.en: For sure. It's also work because I have to show up.
sentences.zh: 当然。那也是工作，因为我必须准时出现。

sentences.en: If you commit to be somewhere at a certain time, that's work.
sentences.zh: 如果你承诺在某个时间出现在某个地方，那就是工作。

sentences.en: Because that morning I might wake up and think, I don't really want to do that today.
sentences.zh: 因为那天早上我醒来时可能会想，我今天真的不想做那件事。

sentences.en: But it's agreed to with other people. I'm going to be at this place and we're going to do this thing, so I have to show up.
sentences.zh: 但这是和其他人约定好的。我要去那个地方，我们要一起做这件事，所以我必须到场。

sentences.en: But most days, I don't want to do the things that I'm scheduled to do.
sentences.zh: 但大多数时候，我并不想做那些我预定要做的事情。

sentences.en: That's shocking to me, though. At the time that I choose to do them, I want to do them.
sentences.zh: 不过这让我很震惊。在我选择做这些事的时候，我是想做的。

sentences.en: I know I want to do them, but still, it's really nice not to have to get out of bed, or it's nice to go for a walk on the beach.
sentences.zh: 我知道我想做，但即便如此，不用起床或者去海滩散散步还是很舒服的。

sentences.en: So I think I might be well positioned. This is, I'm just now getting advice from you because I'm a huge fan of you, and I respect the way you think.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我可能处于一个很好的位置。这是……我现在正从你那里获得建议，因为我是你的忠实粉丝，我很尊重你的思维方式。

sentences.en: Anyways, I just did another podcast on the book you wrote, Creative Act, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，我刚刚又听了一遍你写的书《Creative Act》的播客。

sentences.en: And there's so many ideas that you put into words that are in my head that I didn't have words for in there.
sentences.zh: 你用文字表达了许多我脑海中存在、但却无法用语言形容的想法。

sentences.en: So if I, right now, I feel like this is, I don't work a day in my life.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我现在感觉，我这一生中没有一天是在工作。

sentences.en: I feel like I wake up and I'm like compelled or like I don't even know the word to use it like then there's no doubt that I'm just on the right path if I was sitting here and we weren't recording and I was just seeking your advice like I don't feel it's at work at all the only time it feels like work is when I have to edit which I fucking hate but I do it anyways because I think it makes it better yeah but that's the only example it's a good example there are parts of it that are not always fun.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我醒来时，就像是被某种力量驱使，或者我甚至不知道该用什么词来形容。毫无疑问，我正走在正确的道路上。如果我坐在这里，我们没有在录音，我只是在寻求你的建议，我一点也不觉得这是在工作。唯一感觉像工作的时候是必须剪辑的时候，我他妈讨厌剪辑，但我还是会做，因为我觉得这会让作品更好。是的，但这只是个例子，这确实是个好例子，工作中总有些部分是不那么有趣的。

sentences.en: And when you're committing time. Like time is our most valuable resource.
sentences.zh: 而且当你投入时间时。时间是我们最宝贵的资源。

sentences.en: And when we're committing our time to doing something in advance, which we do, we pre-schedule, the day of, you don't always want to do that thing.
sentences.zh: 当我们提前承诺投入时间去做某事时，也就是我们预先安排好的时候，你并不总是想做那件事。

sentences.en: But I feel you have complete control over your time and your life.
sentences.zh: 但我感觉你对自己的时间和生活有完全的掌控权。

sentences.en: Yes. How are you still? I choose it. And I have to acknowledge, no one's forcing me to do this.
sentences.zh: 是的。你为什么还能保持这样？我选择了它。我必须承认，没有人强迫我做这些。

sentences.en: I said I would show up. I have to show up.
sentences.zh: 我说过我会到场。我就必须到场。

sentences.en: But in your day-to-day, that still feels like work.
sentences.zh: 但在你的日常生活中，那仍然感觉像是工作。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's like I'd be happy not doing anything.
sentences.zh: 是的，如果什么都不做，我会很开心。

sentences.en: Well, I don't know. I don't know if that's true.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道。我不知道那是不是真的。

sentences.en: There's no way. It's never been the case.
sentences.zh: 不可能。从来没有过那种情况。

sentences.en: I've always. Because you could have stopped working decades ago.
sentences.zh: 我一直……因为你几十年前就可以停止工作了。

sentences.en: Yes. And I think you're addicted to making great shit.
sentences.zh: 是的。而且我觉得你对创作出色的作品上瘾了。

sentences.en: Yes. And I'm lazy. It's a real part of it.
sentences.zh: 是的。而且我很懒。这是真实的一部分。

sentences.en: I'm telling you an honest piece of this, which is every day.
sentences.zh: 我是在诚实地告诉你其中的一部分，那就是每一天。

sentences.en: It's not like, let's go. Every day it's like, oh, no, I got to go work.
sentences.zh: 并不是说，冲啊。每一天都是，哦，不，我得去工作了。

sentences.en: You're disappointing me. I'm sad. I'm sad.
sentences.zh: 你让我失望了。我很伤心。我很伤心。

sentences.en: But it doesn't feel like it feels like out of almost anybody in the world that gets paid for being them.
sentences.zh: 但这感觉不像……感觉像是世界上几乎没有谁能因为做自己而获得报酬。

sentences.en: Yeah. Is you. Yes. And you're saying that's not the case.
sentences.zh: 是的。是你。是的。而你说情况并非如此。

sentences.en: No, I'm me. I'm definitely me. There is a part of me that doesn't want to show up for anything.
sentences.zh: 不，我就是我。我绝对是我。我内心有一部分是不想为任何事情露面的。

sentences.en: And I have to overcome that every day. That's what I'm saying.
sentences.zh: 我每天都必须克服这一点。这就是我想说的。

sentences.en: Did you ever spend any time with Tony Bourdain when he was alive?
sentences.zh: 你生前和Tony Bourdain相处过吗？

sentences.en: Never have. Were you ever a fan of any of his?
sentences.zh: 从来没有。你是他的粉丝吗？

sentences.en: Yeah. Okay. So I read all his books, watch all his shows.
sentences.zh: 是的。好吧。我读过他所有的书，看过他所有的节目。

sentences.en: And in his book, I was shocked because that guy, first of all, like in his book, he describes what it's like to be a heroin addict, which is insane.
sentences.zh: 在他的书里，我很震惊，因为那个家伙，首先，他在书里描述了作为一个海洛因成瘾者是什么感觉，这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: And the amount, what you realize when you read Kitchen Confidential is like the same work ethic he used to score drugs as a junk, as a broke junkie.
sentences.zh: 当你读《Kitchen Confidential》时，你会意识到他作为一个身无分文的瘾君子为了搞到毒品所用的职业道德，和他后来写书、制作电视节目时用的是一样的。

sentences.en: Once he broke that habit, he just applied it to writing and building TV shows.
sentences.zh: 一旦他戒掉了那个习惯，他就把它应用到了写作和制作电视节目上。

sentences.en: Like his work ethic was the same, which was directed at the worst thing possible, being a fucking heroin addict.
sentences.zh: 他的职业道德是一样的，只不过之前被用在了最糟糕的事情上，也就是做一个该死的海洛因瘾君子。

sentences.en: And then he directed in a positive generative direction and he took off.
sentences.zh: 然后他把它引向了一个积极的、创造性的方向，然后他就起飞了。

sentences.en: But he said something very similar to you.
sentences.zh: 但他说的和你非常相似。

sentences.en: He's like somewhere deep inside me is this guy that just wants to smoke weed and lay in bed all day.
sentences.zh: 他说，在我内心深处，有这样一个家伙，只想抽大麻，整天躺在床上。

sentences.en: And he goes, I have to fight. His writing is beautiful.
sentences.zh: 他说，我必须战斗。他的文字很美。

sentences.en: He's like, I have to fight that guy every single day.
sentences.zh: 他说，我每天都必须和那个家伙战斗。

sentences.en: Yeah. Now, what's also true, I do have to fight that guy to show up.
sentences.zh: 是的。现在，同样真实的是，我也必须和那个家伙战斗才能准时出现。

sentences.en: And there are parts of the job that are just like watching paint dry, waiting for something good to happen.
sentences.zh: 工作中有些部分就像看着油漆变干一样，等待着好事情发生。

sentences.en: But that moment of magic when something good does happen is the thing I'm addicted to. that feeling of it wasn't good, it's not good, oh my God, it's good.
sentences.zh: 但当好事情发生时，那一刻的魔力就是我上瘾的东西。那种感觉从‘不好，不怎么样’到‘天哪，太棒了’。

sentences.en: And it's like a miracle because nobody knows how or why that happened.
sentences.zh: 这就像一个奇迹，因为没人知道它是怎么发生的，或者为什么会发生。

sentences.en: It's not in our control. That's the other thing about it.
sentences.zh: 这不在我们的控制范围内。这也是关于它的另一件事。

sentences.en: It really is magic. So I'm addicted to the magic part of it, but I'm not addicted to everything leading up to those magical moments.
sentences.zh: 它确实是魔法。所以我对魔法部分上瘾，但我对通往那些神奇时刻之前的一切并不上瘾。

sentences.en: I'm patient. I'm patient enough to wait forever for that thing to happen. but it's not fun.
sentences.zh: 我有耐心。我有足够的耐心去等待那件事发生。但这并不有趣。

sentences.en: Like some people really look forward to fishing.
sentences.zh: 就像有些人真的很期待钓鱼。

sentences.en: It's like fishing. It's like you can go out and spend a whole day fishing and not catch any fish.
sentences.zh: 这就像钓鱼。你可以出去钓一整天的鱼，却什么也钓不到。

sentences.en: It's like that. You can work in the studio for a day or for a week and nothing good can happen.
sentences.zh: 就是那样。你可以在录音室工作一天或一周，什么好结果都不会发生。

sentences.en: That happens. It's out of our control. But when the good thing happens, it's like, ah, there it is.
sentences.zh: 这种情况会发生。这不在我们的控制范围内。但当好事情发生时，就像是，啊，它就在那儿。

sentences.en: That's why we're here. That fishing analogy is really important to me.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在这里的原因。那个钓鱼的比喻对我来说非常重要。

sentences.en: I've heard you say this a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 几年前我听你这么说过。

sentences.en: It's the best example. I heard Akon one time describe working with Eminem.
sentences.zh: 这是最好的例子。我曾经听Akon描述过和Eminem一起工作。

sentences.en: And he shows up into Detroit and he gives them a call.
sentences.zh: 他来到底特律，给他们打了个电话。

sentences.en: He's like, all right, I figure we're going to do a night session.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，我想我们要做个夜场。

sentences.en: You know, these guys are usually nocturnal.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些家伙通常是夜行性的。

sentences.en: Calls them at like 7 p.m. And Em's like, yeah, I'll see you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 他在晚上7点左右打电话给他们。Em说，好吧，明天见。

sentences.en: And Akon's like, tomorrow? Like, what are you talking about?
sentences.zh: Akon说，明天？你在说什么？

sentences.en: Shows up and doesn't realize that he treats it like a job.
sentences.zh: 他出现时才意识到，他把这当作一份工作。

sentences.en: Shows up at 9 a.m. He's in the studio writing, like you're saying, recording verses.
sentences.zh: 他早上9点就到了。他像你说的，在录音室里写歌、录制歌词。

sentences.en: I think it's like, let's say noon. He literally be in the middle of a verse.
sentences.zh: 我想大概是中午吧。他正写到一半。

sentences.en: They're like, oh, I'll be right back. I'm going to take lunch.
sentences.zh: 他们说，哦，我马上回来。我要去吃午饭。

sentences.en: And he's like, what? Goes, comes back at one, goes back to work at five o'clock.
sentences.zh: 他说，什么？他回来后，五点钟又回去工作。

sentences.en: Says, all right, I'll see you the next day.
sentences.zh: 说，好吧，明天见。

sentences.en: And people like misunderstood what Akon was saying.
sentences.zh: 人们误解了Akon的意思。

sentences.en: It's like, he doesn't wait around for inspiration.
sentences.zh: 他是说，他不会坐等灵感。

sentences.en: He shows up every day knowing that if he does the work, then it will come.
sentences.zh: 他每天都出现，因为他知道如果他付出了努力，灵感就会到来。

sentences.en: Yes. It's exactly what you're saying about fishing.
sentences.zh: 是的。这和你说的钓鱼完全一样。

sentences.en: Yeah. And inspiration is a real thing too, but it's both.
sentences.zh: 是的。灵感确实存在，但两者缺一不可。

sentences.en: Like if you only wait for inspiration, it won't ever come.
sentences.zh: 如果你只等待灵感，它永远不会到来。

sentences.en: You have to work and be there and show up.
sentences.zh: 你必须工作，必须在那里，必须准时出现。

sentences.en: If you're not in the practice of allowing the thing to happen, it won't happen.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有养成让事情发生的习惯，它就不会发生。

sentences.en: Doesn't mean it will. Just because you do show up doesn't mean it will happen.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着它一定会发生。仅仅因为你出现了，并不意味着它一定会发生。

sentences.en: But if you don't show up, it won't happen.
sentences.zh: 但如果你不出现，它就绝对不会发生。

sentences.en: You got me into Johnny Cash, who is a couple of generations before me.
sentences.zh: 你让我迷上了Johnny Cash，他比我早了几代人。

sentences.en: And not only was the music great, but I loved you describing what went into making it. we can talk about that but there was something like a the way i would like uh still down what you were saying is like constraints are actually your friend yeah if you don't like you can't do everything so if you if you artificially constrain yourself you can't you it forces you to be more creative can you talk about this i feel like you've used this a bunch in your career yeah it's like the idea of creating a palette and the albums that speak to me most are ones when you hear them, you know, if an artist has 20 albums, but you hear a song, you know, oh, that has to be on that album, that seventh album, because that's the only album that sounds like that.
sentences.zh: 不仅音乐很棒，而且我很喜欢你描述制作过程的方式。我们可以谈谈那个，但你所说的有一种……我把它总结为‘限制其实是你的朋友’。是的，如果你不喜欢……你不能做所有事情，所以如果你人为地限制自己，它会迫使你更有创造力。你能谈谈这个吗？我觉得你在职业生涯中多次使用过这个方法。

sentences.en: Even though the band always sounds like the band, this group of songs sounds different than all the rest.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就像创造调色板的想法。那些最打动我的专辑，当你听到它们时，你知道，如果一个艺术家有20张专辑，但你听到一首歌，你知道，哦，那一定是在那张专辑里，那第七张专辑，因为那是唯一听起来像那样的专辑。

sentences.en: And it may be that it was either recorded in a different way, or all the songs were about a particular thing or they're using different instrumentation than they used to use.
sentences.zh: 即使乐队听起来总是像那个乐队，但这组歌曲听起来和其他所有歌曲都不同。

sentences.en: I like it when an album like stands alone outside of an artist's career as a defining moment in time.
sentences.zh: 这可能是因为它以不同的方式录制，或者所有的歌都是关于特定的事情，或者他们使用了与以往不同的乐器。

sentences.en: It's not just more of the same. But how is that tied to these constraints that you put on the work?
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一张专辑在艺术家的职业生涯之外，作为一个定义性的时刻独立存在。

sentences.en: That happens by coming up with like a series of rules that only apply to this project.
sentences.zh: 它不仅仅是更多相同的东西。但这和你施加在作品上的这些限制有什么联系？

sentences.en: Those are the constraints. So that could be...
sentences.zh: 这是通过提出一系列仅适用于该项目的规则来实现的。

sentences.en: In the Johnny Cash example. In Johnny Cash's case, the first one was, I didn't know that it was going to be an acoustic album, which it turned out to be.
sentences.zh: 这就是限制。所以这可能是……

sentences.en: But that was something that through the process of recording, I learned the most interesting version of this to me is when he's singing alone, which is really the demos in my living room, him singing me songs.
sentences.zh: 以Johnny Cash为例。在Johnny Cash的案例中，第一个限制是，我当时不知道它会是一张原声专辑，但结果确实是。

sentences.en: That sounded better than when we went into the recording studio with musicians and played them with the band.
sentences.zh: 但这是我在录音过程中学到的，对我来说，最有趣的版本是他独自演唱的时候，也就是我在客厅里录的小样，他为我唱那些歌。

sentences.en: And it wasn't as interesting. I didn't know that in advance.
sentences.zh: 那听起来比我们走进录音室，和音乐家们一起用乐队伴奏录制时要好。

sentences.en: That wasn't a premeditated idea. And then in terms of the material that he would sing, I grew up with this image.
sentences.zh: 而且没那么有趣。我事先并不知道这一点。

sentences.en: What spoke to me about Johnny Cash was this image of the man in black.
sentences.zh: 那不是一个预谋的想法。然后就他要唱的素材而言，我是伴随着这个形象长大的。

sentences.en: And the man in black is a mythical character.
sentences.zh: 打动我的是Johnny Cash身上‘黑衣人’的形象。

sentences.en: Yes, Johnny Cash, but it's not just Johnny Cash.
sentences.zh: 黑衣人是一个神话般的人物。

sentences.en: It's like the mythical Johnny Cash, the Johnny Cash who's the man in black. and the man Johnny Cash could sing a funny song.
sentences.zh: 是的，Johnny Cash，但这不仅仅是Johnny Cash。

sentences.en: The man in black probably wouldn't sing a funny song.
sentences.zh: 这就像神话中的Johnny Cash，那个作为黑衣人的Johnny Cash。而Johnny Cash本人可以唱一首有趣的歌。

sentences.en: So the material that we picked was always through the eyes of what's something that man in black, the legendary mythological character, what would he sing?
sentences.zh: 黑衣人可能不会唱有趣的歌。

sentences.en: And those are the songs that we chose. And so in this case, the constraints are you, Johnny, a guitar.
sentences.zh: 所以我们选择的素材总是通过‘那个黑衣人，那个传奇的神话角色，他会唱什么？’的视角来决定的。

sentences.en: I think he said he didn't even use a pick.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们选择的歌曲。所以在这种情况下，限制就是你、Johnny和一把吉他。

sentences.en: It was like his fingers. Every guitar, every time he strung the guitar was his fingers.
sentences.zh: 我想他说他甚至没用拨片。

sentences.en: And you guys in a house. Yeah, but a big part of it too is the choice of material.
sentences.zh: 就像是用他的手指。每次他拨动吉他，都是用他的手指。

sentences.en: That's a big part of it for those albums.
sentences.zh: 你们在房子里。是的，但很大一部分也是素材的选择。

sentences.en: And it's looked at through the viewpoint of not a funny song, but a man in black will do this.
sentences.zh: 这对那些专辑来说是很重要的一部分。

sentences.en: And not even just a funny song. It had to have a certain amount of gravitas to fit a mythical character singing it.
sentences.zh: 它是通过不是‘一首有趣的歌’，而是‘黑衣人会做这个’的视角来看待的。

sentences.en: When I think about everything I've read about you and as much as I've heard you speak, I feel like you would agree with the statement that great things can't be made by a committee.
sentences.zh: 甚至不仅仅是关于有趣的歌。它必须有一定的庄重感，才能符合一个神话人物演唱它的身份。

sentences.en: Correct. It would be unusual for that to be the case.
sentences.zh: 当我想到我读过的关于你的一切，以及我听过你说的那么多话，我觉得你会同意‘伟大的事物不能由委员会创造’这一说法。

sentences.en: In many cases, it's just, there could be a band.
sentences.zh: 没错。这种情况很少见。

sentences.en: It tends to water it down. It tends to water it down.
sentences.zh: 在很多情况下，可能只是有一个乐队。

sentences.en: So this is the case in companies, since obviously my main focus is on entrepreneurship.
sentences.zh: 这往往会稀释它。这往往会稀释它。

sentences.en: Yeah. It's like, even if there is a group, there's usually like a main person.
sentences.zh: 所以在公司里也是如此，因为显然我的主要关注点是创业。

sentences.en: Is that the same thing in bands? Is there always like one, like there might be four guys in the band or five guys in the band.
sentences.zh: 是的。就像，即使有一个团队，通常也会有一个主要负责人。

sentences.en: Is it usually the stronger personality that has more influence?
sentences.zh: 乐队也是一样吗？通常总是有一个……乐队里可能有四五个人。

sentences.en: In a band, what makes a band great is how the different musicians hear music and play together.
sentences.zh: 通常是更强势的人更有影响力吗？

sentences.en: And it doesn't have to be a single point of view.
sentences.zh: 在乐队里，让乐队变得伟大的是不同的音乐家如何聆听音乐并一起演奏。

sentences.en: The Beatles are a great example because John and Paul really were very different people and wrote different kinds of songs and approached music in different ways.
sentences.zh: 它不一定非得是一个单一的观点。

sentences.en: Jagger and Richards, same. There's opposition there.
sentences.zh: The Beatles就是一个很好的例子，因为John和Paul确实是非常不同的人，写不同类型的歌，以不同的方式处理音乐。

sentences.en: That goes against exactly what you said.
sentences.zh: Jagger和Richards也是一样。他们之间存在对立。

sentences.en: It's a different model. But then like in Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers, Tom Petty is really the flag bearer of the band.
sentences.zh: 这和你刚才说的完全相反。

sentences.en: And everyone lines up behind Tom. They're all great.
sentences.zh: 这是另一种模式。但就像在Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers里，Tom Petty确实是乐队的旗手。

sentences.en: And they all can play great things. And they all add incredible things.
sentences.zh: 每个人都排在Tom后面。他们都很棒。

sentences.en: But Tom is sort of the final word in what happens in that band.
sentences.zh: 他们都能演奏出色的东西。他们都增加了不可思议的东西。

sentences.en: In a band like U2, it's democratic. Everybody in the band has to like it.
sentences.zh: 但Tom在乐队里发生的事情上拥有最终决定权。

sentences.en: If three of the guys like it and one of the guys doesn't, it doesn't happen.
sentences.zh: 在像U2这样的乐队里，它是民主的。乐队里的每个人都必须喜欢它。

sentences.en: And that's another model that works for them.
sentences.zh: 如果三个人喜欢，而其中一个人不喜欢，它就不会发生。

sentences.en: So if we go back to this designing in constraints, your work with Johnny Cash is very simple.
sentences.zh: 这是另一种对他们有效的模式。

sentences.en: Go back all the way 40 years before that.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们回到这种在限制中设计的方法，你和Johnny Cash的工作非常简单。

sentences.en: I'm reducing. I'm not producing. I think in 2023, I listened to, I don't know, 600 to 700 individual.
sentences.zh: 回到那之前的40年。

sentences.en: I listened to two or three podcast episodes a day.
sentences.zh: 我在做减法。我不是在制作。我想在2023年，我听了，我不知道，600到700个个人节目。

sentences.en: So, I don't know, 700, 900 episodes. I think the single best podcast episode that I listened to all that year was your episode on Tetragrammaton with Jimmy Iovine.
sentences.zh: 我每天听两到三集播客。

sentences.en: There was a story that you told in there that was very fascinating because Jimmy's like, I think, 10 years older than you, kind of like 10 years.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不知道，700到900集。我认为我那一年听过的最好的单集播客就是你在Tetragrammaton上和Jimmy Iovine的那一集。

sentences.en: Almost exactly 10 years older. We're a day where our birthdays are a day apart.
sentences.zh: 你在里面讲了一个非常迷人的故事，因为Jimmy比你大10岁，大概10岁。

sentences.en: Yeah. And you tell this phenomenal story on the podcast of one of the first, maybe the first time you met Jimmy Iovine, he said something that was so strange.
sentences.zh: 几乎正好大10岁。我们的生日只差一天。

sentences.en: You go to play something you're working on.
sentences.zh: 是的。你在播客里讲了一个非凡的故事，关于你第一次见到Jimmy Iovine时，他说了些非常奇怪的话。

sentences.en: Yeah. And he goes, I wish I could still make something that simple.
sentences.zh: 你去播放你正在制作的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah. And your response was, I'm sure you can.
sentences.zh: 是的。他说，我希望我还能做出那么简单的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, what do you mean? Explain why he said that and what's happening, what happens over time.
sentences.zh: 是的。你的回答是，我相信你可以。

sentences.en: Yeah, because he was a producer.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是什么意思？解释一下他为什么这么说，以及随着时间的推移发生了什么。

sentences.en: And as you learn more of what you can do, you tend to do that.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为他是一位制作人。

sentences.en: They tend to get bigger. At that point in time, I hadn't done it enough.
sentences.zh: 当你学到更多你能做的事情时，你往往会去尝试。它们往往会变得越来越大。在那个时候，我做得还不够多。

sentences.en: It was my first record. So that was the Cult Electric was my first rock record.
sentences.zh: 那是我的第一张唱片。所以那是The Cult的《Electric》，是我的第一张摇滚唱片。

sentences.en: This is after almost a decade in hip-hop or half a decade in hip-hop?
sentences.zh: 这是在近十年或半个十年的嘻哈音乐之后吗？

sentences.en: No. No? No. When was this? Same. Like, same time.
sentences.zh: 不。不是吗？不。这是什么时候？同样。就像，同一时间。

sentences.en: Oh, okay, okay. Yeah, this is like 19...
sentences.zh: 哦，好的，好的。是的，这是19……

sentences.en: Is this when you moved to California? No, this is still in New York.
sentences.zh: 这是你搬到加州的时候吗？不，这还在纽约。

sentences.en: Oh, shit. Okay, so give me this. I'm still living in the dorm.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。好的，告诉我这个。我当时还住在宿舍里。

sentences.en: I'm still living in the dorm at NYU. Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 我还在纽约大学的宿舍里。哦，天哪。

sentences.en: I thought this was... Okay, so this is the very beginning.
sentences.zh: 我以为这是……好的，所以这是最开始的时候。

sentences.en: So it's as simple as it gets because that's all you can do.
sentences.zh: 所以它尽可能简单，因为那就是你能做的全部。

sentences.en: Yeah, I was doing what I was very simple, but I stayed true to that as much as I can.
sentences.zh: 是的，我做的事情非常简单，但我尽可能地保持真实。

sentences.en: There have probably been a couple of examples along the way where I may have not stayed true.
sentences.zh: 一路上可能有一两个例子我可能没有保持真实。

sentences.en: Very few, if you look at my whole recorded discography, there may be two or three examples where it got out of control or where the artists that I'm working with just had a very different vision, which does happen sometimes and usually we end up not working together again.
sentences.zh: 非常少，如果你看我整个录制的唱片目录，可能只有两三个例子是失控的，或者我合作的艺术家有完全不同的愿景，这种情况确实有时会发生，通常我们最后就不会再合作了。

sentences.en: And there have been one or two occasions where we end up not even finishing a work because it's just too, we just see it in a different way.
sentences.zh: 有一两次我们甚至没有完成作品，因为我们只是太……我们只是以不同的方式看待它。

sentences.en: I had that experience with Joe Cocker. We went into the studio to record and I had a specific vision of how I saw Joe Cocker and what I thought was great about Joe Cocker.
sentences.zh: 我和Joe Cocker有过那样的经历。我们走进录音室录音，我对Joe Cocker有特定的愿景，我认为Joe Cocker伟大之处在于什么。

sentences.en: And he really had a vision of it being something different than that.
sentences.zh: 而他确实有一个与此不同的愿景。

sentences.en: And we weren't on the same page and it didn't drive.
sentences.zh: 我们不在同一个频道上，没有达成共识。

sentences.en: So it never happened. I'm curious your perspective since you've known Jimmy Iovine for so long because he has a very, another singular career where he like kind of in music the whole time, but jumped around.
sentences.zh: 所以它从未发生。我很好奇你的观点，因为你认识Jimmy Iovine这么久了，因为他有另一个独特的职业生涯，他一直在音乐领域，但跳来跳去。
