sentences.en: Yeah, different job from, you know, engineer to producer to record company owner to then building businesses with his artists.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这和从工程师到制作人，再到唱片公司老板，最后和艺人一起创业，完全是不同的工作。

sentences.en: Like what do you think is special about him?
sentences.zh: 你觉得他身上有什么特别之处？

sentences.en: Like what's unique about him? Why was he able to do what he was able to do?
sentences.zh: 他有什么独特的地方？为什么他能做到他所做到的那些事？

sentences.en: He's got good taste and he's got a great work ethic.
sentences.zh: 他品味很好，而且工作极其敬业。

sentences.en: Those are the two. To me, in my mind, you two are very almost, before this conversation I'm having with you, almost at the opposite ends of the spectrum, where I felt like you were just like drawn, you know, like a moth to a flame about what you want to do.
sentences.zh: 就这两点。在我看来，在今天和你谈话之前，我觉得你们俩几乎处于光谱的两端。我觉得你就像飞蛾扑火一样，被自己想做的事情所吸引。

sentences.en: Where he's like, it was always work. I never liked it.
sentences.zh: 而他呢，对他来说，那一直都是工作。我从来没喜欢过它。

sentences.en: It was always a job. I like certain parts of it, but he essentially just forced himself to do it.
sentences.zh: 那一直只是一份工作。我喜欢其中的某些部分，但他本质上只是强迫自己去完成它。

sentences.en: He said something really interesting that I thought really summed it up, which was Jimmy is in the banking business.
sentences.zh: 他说过一件很有意思的事，我觉得总结得很到位，那就是Jimmy是在做银行业务。

sentences.en: These are his words. He said, I'm in the banking business and you're in the church business.
sentences.zh: 这是他的原话。他说，我在做银行业务，而你在做教会业务。

sentences.en: And that's the difference. Explain that.
sentences.zh: 这就是区别。解释一下。

sentences.en: I love this. It's that I'm doing a passion and belief, and he's doing a bottom line, what's going to work?
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个说法。意思是我在追求热情和信仰，而他在追求底线，追求什么能行得通？

sentences.en: What's going to be good for business? And it's just two different things, two different mentalities.
sentences.zh: 什么对生意有利？这就是两码事，两种完全不同的心态。

sentences.en: There's a great line in The Defiant Ones where he hears, he's producing Tom Petty, and he hears a song.
sentences.zh: 在《The Defiant Ones》里有一句很棒的台词，当时他在制作Tom Petty的专辑，他听到了一首歌。

sentences.en: He goes, this is house music. And Tom goes, what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 他说，这是浩室音乐（house music）。Tom问，你什么意思？

sentences.en: He goes, he goes, find me, you know, whatever, eight more albums.
sentences.zh: 他说，去给我找，你知道的，再找八张专辑来。

sentences.en: He goes, that song's going to buy you a house. yeah so that it's we have a different we have a we're different in that way and tom goes i've never heard somebody describe music that way like this is gonna buy me a house yeah there's a bunch of stories that jimmy uh tells in that um podcast with you about the crazy things that you see in the music business you know where uh i think he tells a story like the phil specter coming to the studio with like a butcher's uh in a butcher's outfit and he's got like guns strapped to him everywhere and david geffen's in the studio and john lennon's getting drunk do you have any like things that stand out from you i've never heard you here tell any of these like stories of stuff you've seen inside the studio i can remember doing a session with odb old dirty bastard from wu-tang and i remember being nervous because i'd never met him before and his reputation preceded him so i didn't really know what i was going into and um and i thought i'm gonna i'm to bring my dog i had a pulley which is a dog that has dreadlocks and i'll be and that would be whatever's going on if you see a dog with dreadlocks it's interesting like it it it doesn't it's fascinating in its own way and i had a friend of mine also filming everything because i thought well if there's a camera and if there's a dog it's going to be okay What was his reputation for you to do this though?
sentences.zh: 他说，那首歌能帮你买套房。是的，所以我们在这方面确实不同。Tom说，我从没听过有人这样描述音乐，说这首歌能帮我买套房。确实，Jimmy在和你录的那期播客里讲了很多故事，关于你在音乐圈见过的那些疯狂事。比如他讲到Phil Specter穿着屠夫装来到录音室，身上到处绑着枪，David Geffen也在录音室里，John Lennon喝得烂醉。你有什么印象深刻的事吗？我从没听你讲过这些在录音室里见到的事。我记得有一次和Wu-Tang的ODB（Old Dirty Bastard）录音，我当时很紧张，因为我之前没见过他，他的名声在外，所以我不知道会发生什么。我想，我要带上我的狗，我有一只波利犬，那种长着脏辫的狗。我想，不管发生什么，如果你看到一只长着脏辫的狗，那会很有趣，它本身就很迷人。我还让我的一个朋友把一切都拍下来，因为我想，如果有摄像机，还有一只狗，应该会没事的。不过他当时的名声到底是怎么样的，让你需要做这些准备？

sentences.en: All kinds of crazy things like... Violence?
sentences.zh: 各种疯狂的事情，比如……暴力？

sentences.en: Could be violence, could be a lot of things that would not be good.
sentences.zh: 可能是暴力，也可能是很多其他不好的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah. And just things I wasn't really prepared for.
sentences.zh: 是的。还有一些我完全没准备好的事情。

sentences.en: But I loved him. You know, I was a fan. And I remember we walked in and he looked and he pointed at the dog and he said, he's okay.
sentences.zh: 但我很喜欢他。你知道，我是他的粉丝。我记得我们走进去时，他看了看，指着狗说，它没问题。

sentences.en: And then he pointed at the camera, he's got to go.
sentences.zh: 然后他指着摄像机说，它得走。

sentences.en: It's like, okay. And then he went and then the session ended up going pretty well.
sentences.zh: 就像是，好吧。然后他就走了，那次录音最后进行得还挺顺利。

sentences.en: We mentioned Toby Luque earlier. And in the conversation I had with him that was very fascinating, he said something where he's just like, there's not like one right way to do things.
sentences.zh: 我们之前提到了Toby Luque。在我和他那次非常精彩的谈话中，他说了一句话，大意是做事没有唯一的正确方法。

sentences.en: There's probably a hundred, which I think you would agree with.
sentences.zh: 可能有上百种，我想你会同意这一点。

sentences.en: And he's like, you just have to find the one that fits best for you and just do that.
sentences.zh: 他说，你只需要找到最适合你的那一种，然后去做就行了。

sentences.en: And you would think this like German computer programmer engineer would be like very rigid.
sentences.zh: 你可能会觉得这个德国计算机程序员工程师会非常刻板。

sentences.en: But when you talk to him, he essentially just runs his life by all intuition.
sentences.zh: 但当你和他交谈时，你会发现他本质上完全是凭直觉在生活。

sentences.en: You are all intuition. All intuition. like explain like why you essentially your entire life is just is in my opinion like managed or or run by just into intuitive feelings yeah i've always been true to what i feel and it's worked out i suppose if it didn't work out then maybe i would have to try something else but it's the fact that I've stayed true to what feels right to me, and luckily, by the grace of God, it has resonated with other people, it allows me to continue doing it.
sentences.zh: 你完全是凭直觉。完全凭直觉。解释一下为什么你的人生本质上，在我看来，是被直觉所引导或驱动的。是的，我一直忠于自己的感觉，而且我想这奏效了。如果没奏效，也许我就得尝试别的方法了。但事实是我坚持了自己觉得对的事情，幸运的是，承蒙上帝眷顾，它引起了其他人的共鸣，这让我能够继续做下去。

sentences.en: But I suppose if that didn't happen, I would just make things for myself on a small level and keep doing it and have a real job.
sentences.zh: 但我想如果没发生这种情况，我可能就会在小范围内为自己做点东西，继续做下去，然后找份正经工作。

sentences.en: Is this your guided by intuition tied to, I feel you have a skepticism of human knowledge.
sentences.zh: 这种被直觉引导的方式，是否和你对人类知识的怀疑有关？

sentences.en: I think you say, like, I think we know very little about everything.
sentences.zh: 我想你是说，我觉得我们对一切都知之甚少。

sentences.en: Thomas Edison has this famous quote where he's like, we don't know one one thousandth percent of anything.
sentences.zh: 托马斯·爱迪生有句名言，他说我们对任何事物的了解连千分之一都不到。

sentences.en: Yeah. I believe that. I believe we don't know anything.
sentences.zh: 是的。我相信这一点。我相信我们什么都不知道。

sentences.en: Yeah. So if you believe you don't know anything, then what is the only other thing you could do is be guided by your intuition.
sentences.zh: 是的。所以如果你相信自己什么都不知道，那么你唯一能做的就是听从直觉。

sentences.en: Yeah. And to try things and see what works.
sentences.zh: 是的。去尝试，看看什么行得通。

sentences.en: And just because one thing works doesn't mean that's the way that, that's the way it happens.
sentences.zh: 而且仅仅因为一件事行得通，并不意味着这就是事情发生的唯一方式。

sentences.en: That's a way that happened to work in that case.
sentences.zh: 那只是在那次情况下恰好行得通的一种方式。

sentences.en: I heard you one time compare and contrast the approach of Jay-Z to Eminem you worked with both of them, can you talk about just how different they are?
sentences.zh: 我听过你对比Jay-Z和Eminem的创作方法，你和他们俩都合作过，能谈谈他们有多不同吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, Em is much more well, he writes down the lyrics and he's really studious in the way that he works and he'll also record take after take after take after it's written and try different things Jay is much more spontaneous.
sentences.zh: 是的，Em要多得多……他会写下歌词，他在工作方式上非常刻苦，而且他会在写完之后一遍又一遍地录音，尝试不同的东西。Jay则要自发得多。

sentences.en: It all happens in his head and then he'll get up and say it once or twice and that's it.
sentences.zh: 一切都在他脑子里完成，然后他会站起来说一两次，就这样了。

sentences.en: What's the energy when you're in the room with both of them though?
sentences.zh: 当你在录音室和他们俩在一起时，那种能量场是什么样的？

sentences.en: M is totally involved in every aspect of everything and Jay is like, play me a bunch of stuff.
sentences.zh: Em完全投入到每一个细节中，而Jay则是，放一堆东西给我听。

sentences.en: If I hear something I like, I'll think about it and if not, I'll see you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 如果我听到喜欢的，我会考虑一下；如果没有，那明天见。

sentences.en: He's like, Jay will only be there when he needs to be there.
sentences.zh: 他就像是，Jay只会在他需要出现的时候出现。

sentences.en: And if you hear something that sparks an idea, he'll sit and just say, play it over and over again, play the music over and over again.
sentences.zh: 如果你放的东西激发了他的灵感，他会坐下来，说，一遍又一遍地放，把音乐一遍又一遍地放。

sentences.en: And he sits in the back and you almost, it goes on long enough where you forget he's even there because he's just silent in the corner, listening, sitting on a couch, listening over and over again.
sentences.zh: 他坐在后面，你几乎……时间久了你都会忘了他在那儿，因为他只是安静地坐在角落里，听着，坐在沙发上，一遍又一遍地听。

sentences.en: 30 minutes, 25 minutes later, I was like, I got it, jumps up.
sentences.zh: 30分钟，25分钟后，他说，我搞定了，然后跳起来。

sentences.en: He runs into the room, hit record. and he does the whole thing just from his head.
sentences.zh: 他冲进录音室，按下录音键。然后他完全凭脑子就把整首歌做完了。

sentences.en: It's amazing. He's the only person I've ever seen do that.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。他是我见过唯一能做到这一点的人。

sentences.en: I think a lot of people know that he did Magna Carta, Holy Grail, essentially in two weeks.
sentences.zh: 我想很多人都知道他做《Magna Carta, Holy Grail》基本上只用了两周。

sentences.en: Like he did the whole album in two weeks.
sentences.zh: 就像他两周内完成了整张专辑。

sentences.en: Most of his albums were made very quickly.
sentences.zh: 他大多数专辑都做得非常快。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was always interesting. He was like, yeah, he recorded them in two weeks, but these ideas he's been refining.
sentences.zh: 是的，这总是很有趣。他就像是，是的，他两周内录完了，但这些想法他一直在打磨。

sentences.en: It's not like when he's not in the studio, he's not thinking about these.
sentences.zh: 并不是说他不在录音室的时候就不在思考这些。

sentences.en: He's like refining these ideas over a long period of time.
sentences.zh: 他是在很长一段时间内不断打磨这些想法。

sentences.en: Sometimes yes, sometimes no. Some of them, it all happens in a weekend. the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 有时是，有时不是。有些歌，整个过程就在一个周末完成了。

sentences.en: That's crazy. Yeah. As opposed to Em, who will work on a song forever.
sentences.zh: 太疯狂了。是的。这和Em形成了对比，Em会为了一首歌工作很久。

sentences.en: Yes. Very different. Just two different styles.
sentences.zh: 是的。非常不同。只是两种不同的风格。

sentences.en: Both amazing. But they just come at it from different, I think it's just different personality types.
sentences.zh: 都很棒。但他们只是从不同的角度切入，我想这只是不同的性格类型。

sentences.en: What do you think Em's personality type is then?
sentences.zh: 那你觉得Em是什么性格类型？

sentences.en: I would describe him as obsessive. You know, he's really perfectionist, willing to do whatever it takes for it to be great. and diligent, hardworking.
sentences.zh: 我会形容他为强迫症。你知道，他真的是个完美主义者，愿意为了做到极致而付出一切。而且勤奋、努力。

sentences.en: And Jay's much more relaxed. Jay's, it just kind of happens for him.
sentences.zh: 而Jay则放松得多。Jay，对他来说，一切都是顺其自然。

sentences.en: He's doing it, but it's just a different style.
sentences.zh: 他在做，但只是风格不同。

sentences.en: Of the two, which one do you think your working style is closer to?
sentences.zh: 在这两者中，你觉得你的工作风格更接近哪一个？

sentences.en: I do a different thing, so it's hard to say.
sentences.zh: 我做的事情不一样，所以很难说。

sentences.en: What I do changes according to who I'm working with.
sentences.zh: 我所做的事情会根据合作对象的不同而改变。

sentences.en: Like whatever the artist needs, is what my job is.
sentences.zh: 艺术家需要什么，我的工作就是什么。

sentences.en: So in some cases, it's totally hands-off.
sentences.zh: 所以在某些情况下，我完全放手。

sentences.en: And in some cases, it's, well, we got to start from the beginning and try to figure this out together.
sentences.zh: 而在某些情况下，我们必须从头开始，试着一起弄清楚。

sentences.en: So you know what I just, I'm thinking of like, it's kind of tied to what you were saying about being a professional listener, that you take a sincere interest in the person, whether you're recording a podcast with them or you're working with them in the studio.
sentences.zh: 你知道我刚才在想什么吗？这和你说的成为一名专业倾听者有关，你对那个人表现出真诚的兴趣，无论你是和他们录播客，还是在录音室里和他们工作。

sentences.en: And so your goal, if I'm reading this correctly, it's just like, has really nothing to do with you.
sentences.zh: 所以你的目标，如果我理解得没错的话，其实和你自己没什么关系。

sentences.en: You feel your act of service to try to get them to be the best version of themselves?
sentences.zh: 你觉得你的服务行为是为了让他们成为最好的自己？

sentences.en: Is that the way you think about it? Yes.
sentences.zh: 你是这样想的吗？是的。

sentences.en: I'd say that's accurate. Do you have anybody that plays that role in your life for you?
sentences.zh: 我想这很准确。你的生活中有人扮演这个角色吗？

sentences.en: I don't know if I do.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我有没有。

sentences.en: I don't know if anyone produces me.
sentences.zh: 我不知道有没有人能制作我。

sentences.en: Could they reduce you? I don't know if there's anything to reduce here.
sentences.zh: 他们能制作你吗？我不知道这里有什么可制作的。

sentences.en: Yeah. I don't know. Luckily, I have friends who, friends and family who are not, particularly interested in what I do.
sentences.zh: 是的。我不知道。幸运的是，我有朋友，有家人，他们对我做的事情并不特别感兴趣。

sentences.en: So I have reality around me a lot of just like, that's crazy.
sentences.zh: 所以我周围有很多现实感，很多那种‘这太疯狂了’的声音。

sentences.en: You know, like a lot of, that's a bad idea.
sentences.zh: 你知道，很多‘这是个坏主意’的声音。

sentences.en: And it's interesting for me because some ideas I hear, that's a bad idea.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说很有趣，因为有些想法我听到后会觉得，那是坏主意。

sentences.en: And it's like, okay, maybe you're right.
sentences.zh: 然后就觉得，好吧，也许你是对的。

sentences.en: And many ideas is like, I'll show you. I'll show you it's a good idea.
sentences.zh: 而很多想法则是，我会证明给你们看。我会证明这是个好主意。

sentences.en: I feel I have to do this, you know. yeah i could see that you take a lot of input but i think you would be resistant to i won't change my mind but i'm open to hearing ideas and definitely open to help if if someone suggests something that makes it better and i see that's like that's the best i'm not closed-minded because someone offers information even experienced wisdom i might not always choose to use that information.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我必须这样做，你知道。是的，我能看出你接受很多建议，但我认为你会抗拒……我不会改变主意，但我乐于听取意见，也绝对乐于在有人提出能让事情变得更好的建议时寻求帮助，我明白那是最好的。我并不是因为有人提供信息，甚至是经验之谈，就思想封闭。我可能并不总是选择使用这些信息。

sentences.en: Do you think you have a big ego? I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 你觉得你自负吗？我不这么认为。

sentences.en: You have a lot of self-confidence though.
sentences.zh: 但你很有自信。

sentences.en: I have a lot of self-confidence. But they even said, somebody met you when they were like 19 and they're like, that's the most self-confident 19-year-old I've ever met.
sentences.zh: 我很有自信。但他们甚至说过，有人在你19岁时见过你，他们说，那是我见过最自信的19岁年轻人。

sentences.en: I think that's the mix. I think, you know, I'm lucky I learned to meditate when I was young and meditation has been a big part of my life.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是那种混合体。我想，你知道，我很幸运，年轻时就学会了冥想，冥想一直是我生活的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: So it's never been about ego. It's never been about me.
sentences.zh: 所以这从来不是关于自我。从来不是关于我。

sentences.en: You know, it's, I'm confident in being able to share what I'm experiencing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我有信心分享我正在经历的事情。

sentences.en: I hear something like, that's amazing. And I hear something else.
sentences.zh: 我听到一些东西，觉得，那太棒了。然后听到另一些东西。

sentences.en: It's like, you know, it's not good enough.
sentences.zh: 就像是，你知道，那还不够好。

sentences.en: And nothing anyone can say will tell me otherwise.
sentences.zh: 无论别人说什么都无法改变我的想法。

sentences.en: It's like, I know I can feel it. So there's confidence in your own judgment.
sentences.zh: 就像是，我知道，我能感觉到。所以这是对自己判断力的自信。

sentences.en: Because you were just saying, you can have somebody who has a lot of experience with them.
sentences.zh: 因为你刚才说，你可以有非常有经验的人在身边。

sentences.en: When I say confidence in my own judgment in, this is how I see it.
sentences.zh: 当我谈到对自己判断力的自信时，是指，我是这样看的。

sentences.en: I'm not saying I'm right. I never say I'm right or I know what's best.
sentences.zh: 我不是说我是对的。我从不说我是对的，或者我知道什么是最好的。

sentences.en: None of those things. This is how I see it.
sentences.zh: 这些都不是。我是这样看的。

sentences.en: I see it clearly. This is how I would vote for it.
sentences.zh: 我看得很清楚。我会这样选择。

sentences.en: If I get to vote, I vote for this.
sentences.zh: 如果我有投票权，我投这一票。

sentences.en: But it's not my way or the highway at all.
sentences.zh: 但这绝不是‘听我的或者滚蛋’。

sentences.en: What is your inner monologue like when you're making something?
sentences.zh: 当你创作时，你的内心独白是什么样的？

sentences.en: Is it positive, negative? Are you self-critical?
sentences.zh: 是积极的，消极的？你自我批判吗？

sentences.en: Depends.
sentences.zh: 看情况。

sentences.en: I would say rarely critical. What it usually is is it starts apprehensive when we start because it could be anything.
sentences.zh: 我会说很少批判。通常情况是，刚开始时会感到忧虑，因为一切皆有可能。

sentences.en: So at first, it's scary. So I don't know what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 所以起初，这很吓人。我不知道会发生什么。

sentences.en: Even today. Even today. And there's usually expectation, because I've had success in the past, that if I'm there, it's going to be great.
sentences.zh: 即使是今天。即使是今天。而且通常会有期望，因为我过去有过成功，所以如果我在场，大家会觉得这一定会很棒。

sentences.en: So I feel this pressure of like, there's expectation.
sentences.zh: 所以我感到了压力，就像，有期望存在。

sentences.en: And I know I can't control anything. It's going to be the way it's going to be.
sentences.zh: 我知道我无法控制任何事情。事情会变成什么样就是什么样。

sentences.en: I know I'm patient. And I know I'll wait until it's great.
sentences.zh: 我知道我有耐心。我知道我会等到它变得很棒为止。

sentences.en: And we start by experimenting and see what it could be.
sentences.zh: 我们从实验开始，看看它能变成什么样。

sentences.en: And as soon as there's a glimmer, as soon as I hear something that's good, then I relax.
sentences.zh: 一旦出现了一丝曙光，一旦我听到了一些好的东西，我就放松了。

sentences.en: But until then, it's too open. You know, it could be too many things.
sentences.zh: 但在那之前，它太开放了。你知道，它可能是太多东西了。

sentences.en: But once something lands, whatever it is, I relax.
sentences.zh: 但一旦有了着落，无论是什么，我就放松了。

sentences.en: It's like, okay, we have at least a direction to move in.
sentences.zh: 就像是，好吧，我们至少有一个前进的方向。

sentences.en: It doesn't mean we stay in that direction forever.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着我们永远保持那个方向。

sentences.en: But having a direction is better than not having a direction.
sentences.zh: 但有一个方向总比没有方向要好。

sentences.en: And when we start, we don't have a direction.
sentences.zh: 当我们开始时，我们没有方向。

sentences.en: So you would say you don't have a self-critical inner monologue constantly playing in your mind?
sentences.zh: 所以你会说你的脑子里没有不断播放的自我批判的内心独白？

sentences.en: Never. It's interesting. The reason I ask you this question is because I was with an entrepreneur yesterday.
sentences.zh: 从来没有。这很有趣。我问你这个问题是因为昨天我和一位企业家在一起。

sentences.en: Guy's worth $10 billion, and he wakes up every morning at 5.30, just assuming he's going out of business.
sentences.zh: 那个人身价100亿美元，他每天早上5点半醒来，都假设自己要破产了。

sentences.en: He's actually paranoid. He lives like a paranoid life, and that's why he thinks he's good.
sentences.zh: 他实际上很偏执。他过着一种偏执的生活，这就是他认为自己优秀的原因。

sentences.en: This is very common with a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 这在很多人身上都很常见。

sentences.en: And I used to have a self-critical, kind of mean.
sentences.zh: 我曾经也有过自我批判，有点刻薄。

sentences.en: I was fucking pretty mean to myself. This guy named Brad Jacobs.
sentences.zh: 我对自己真的很刻薄。有个叫Brad Jacobs的人。

sentences.en: I actually had him on the show. I've talked to him a bunch.
sentences.zh: 我确实请他上过节目。我和他聊过很多次。

sentences.en: And he used to have that too. And now he's in the 60s.
sentences.zh: 他以前也有过这种情况。现在他60多岁了。

sentences.en: It's like, it's counterproductive. It's not helping anything.
sentences.zh: 这适得其反。这没有任何帮助。

sentences.en: And something, I talk about this on the podcast.
sentences.zh: 然后某件事，我在播客里谈过这个。

sentences.en: You can hear me mentioning it over again for a few years.
sentences.zh: 你可以听到我几年里反复提到它。

sentences.en: And just something one day just fucking snapped.
sentences.zh: 有一天，某样东西突然断了。

sentences.en: And I just don't do that anymore. That's great.
sentences.zh: 我就再也不那样做了。那太棒了。

sentences.en: And I went back and I was reading my notes on you.
sentences.zh: 我回去读了关于你的笔记。

sentences.en: And I was just telling my partner, Rob, about this.
sentences.zh: 我刚才还在和我的合伙人Rob谈论这个。

sentences.en: This is the way I look at the work we're doing now.
sentences.zh: 这就是我看待我们现在所做工作的方式。

sentences.en: It's like, I like Rick's framework that like, if you look at your work, it's just like an entry to a diary.
sentences.zh: 就像，我喜欢Rick的框架，即如果你审视你的工作，它就像日记的一页。

sentences.en: Yeah. It's like, there's nothing to be critical about because like you did the best you possibly could have done.
sentences.zh: 是的。没什么可批判的，因为你已经尽了你所能做到的最好。

sentences.en: In that moment. In that moment. Yeah. And then that was 10 years ago and that was five years ago.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻。在那一刻。是的。那是10年前，那是5年前。

sentences.en: And then what we're making today. And I might not do the same thing I would have done 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 然后是我们今天做的东西。我可能不会做我10年前会做的事情。

sentences.en: And that's fine. But I don't have any regrets about 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 那没关系。但我对10年前没有任何遗憾。

sentences.en: That's what I thought. That's real. Each of those installments are real.
sentences.zh: 我就是这么想的。那是真实的。每一份作品都是真实的。

sentences.en: So it's always true. It doesn't mean that that's who you are forever.
sentences.zh: 所以它总是真实的。这并不意味着那就是你永远的样子。

sentences.en: It's who you are in that moment. It's really freeing.
sentences.zh: 那是你在那一刻的样子。这真的很让人解脱。

sentences.en: It's helpful for an artist to think that way.
sentences.zh: 这对艺术家来说是一种很有帮助的思考方式。

sentences.en: Because usually, especially when we're younger, we think the thing that we make is, this is my magnum opus, and this is going to define me for the rest of my life.
sentences.zh: 因为通常，尤其是当我们年轻时，我们认为我们做出的东西是，这是我的代表作，这将定义我的余生。

sentences.en: And it's a daunting hill to climb. But when you realize, it's like, This is just the one today and we're going to make another one tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 这是一座艰巨的山峰。但当你意识到，这只是今天的这一件，明天我们还会做另一件。

sentences.en: And hopefully the one tomorrow is going to be as good or better than the one today.
sentences.zh: 希望明天的那件会和今天的一样好，甚至更好。

sentences.en: What's true today? What's the one? I usually say that if you are excited to share it with your friend, like if I'm working in the studio and long before a record comes out, we're making something. and if someone comes and I'm excited to play it for my friend who has good taste, who I know likes good music, it could come out then.
sentences.zh: 什么是今天真实的？什么是那一件？我通常说，如果你很兴奋能和朋友分享它，比如我在录音室工作，在唱片发行很久之前，我们正在制作东西。如果有人来，我很兴奋能放给我那个品味很好的朋友听，我知道他喜欢好音乐，那它就可以发布了。

sentences.en: Like if I want to play it for them. That's good enough for everybody.
sentences.zh: 就像如果我想放给他们听。这对所有人来说都足够好了。

sentences.en: Do you know what I'm saying? But usually artists will feel like, well, I'll play this for my boys, but it has to be a lot better before regular people can hear it.
sentences.zh: 你知道我在说什么吗？但通常艺术家会觉得，嗯，我会放给哥们听，但在普通人听到之前，它必须变得更好。

sentences.en: And that's ridiculous. It's like as soon as I liked it enough to share it with one person, chances are it's ready for everybody.
sentences.zh: 那太荒谬了。就像我喜欢到足以和一个人分享它时，它很可能就已经准备好面对所有人了。

sentences.en: I've seen you talk to a ton of musicians and artists on camera.
sentences.zh: 我见过你在镜头前和无数音乐家和艺术家交谈。

sentences.en: I just finished rereading this profile that was in Colossus magazine on Josh Kushner.
sentences.zh: 我刚读完《Colossus》杂志上关于Josh Kushner的简介。

sentences.en: And it starts out with him coming to seek your counsel.
sentences.zh: 开头就是他来寻求你的建议。

sentences.en: There's a ton of people that come to seek your counsel.
sentences.zh: 有很多人来寻求你的建议。

sentences.en: And I feel almost like your modus operandi is like holding up a mirror to them and just telling them to do what they know they want to do.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你的行事方式就像是给他们举一面镜子，告诉他们去做他们内心想做的事。

sentences.en: But it's somehow more valuable if they hear it from somebody else.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们从别人那里听到，似乎更有价值。

sentences.en: Does that make any sense to you? Do you resonate with that at all?
sentences.zh: 这说得通吗？你有共鸣吗？

sentences.en: It sounds right. I mean, there are occasions where someone will come to me and say, I'm thinking about doing this crazy thing.
sentences.zh: 听起来是对的。我的意思是，确实有人会来找我，说，我想做这件疯狂的事。

sentences.en: And I'll say, I wonder about that. But more often than not, when people share their hopes and dreams, that's all you need to know.
sentences.zh: 我会说，我对此持保留意见。但更多时候，当人们分享他们的希望和梦想时，这就是你需要知道的一切。

sentences.en: It's like, these are my hopes and dreams, but I'm afraid of this, this, and this.
sentences.zh: 就像是，这些是我的希望和梦想，但我害怕这个、那个，还有那个。

sentences.en: Most often, it's go with the hopes and dreams.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，还是应该追随希望和梦想。

sentences.en: Don't worry about any of that stuff because that stuff doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 别担心那些东西，因为那些东西根本不重要。

sentences.en: What is the stuff that they're afraid of over here?
sentences.zh: 他们害怕的那些东西到底是什么呢？

sentences.en: What someone's going to say. Will I be able to keep doing it?
sentences.zh: 别人会怎么说。我还能继续做下去吗？

sentences.en: My last one was successful. What do I do now?
sentences.zh: 我上一个作品很成功。现在我该做什么？

sentences.en: Success is a funny thing. You know, when you're young and you get successful quickly, no one's prepared for that.
sentences.zh: 成功是一件很有趣的事。你知道，当你年轻时很快就获得了成功，没人能为此做好准备。

sentences.en: And it's awkward and uncomfortable. And you think that's the thing that you want, but when you get it, it's not like what you think it is.
sentences.zh: 这会让人感到尴尬和不自在。你以为那是你想要的，但当你真正得到它时，它并不是你想象的那样。

sentences.en: It's very different. And there are all these pressures that come with it that no one's ready for and no one learns how to do.
sentences.zh: 它非常不同。随之而来的所有压力，没人准备好去应对，也没人学过该怎么处理。

sentences.en: And it's not like whoever you learn good habits from over the course of your life, they don't know how to deal with it because they never got, you know, overnight famous or successful or like it's a weird thing.
sentences.zh: 而且，这不像你人生中从某人那里学到好习惯那样，他们也不知道该怎么处理，因为他们从来没有过那种一夜成名或突然成功的情况，这是一种很奇怪的事情。

sentences.en: So a lot of artists kind of implode in success.
sentences.zh: 所以很多艺术家在成功中崩溃了。

sentences.en: Okay, so I want to ask you why you have not imploded over this many decades.
sentences.zh: 好的，我想问你，为什么你在过去的几十年里没有崩溃？

sentences.en: One of the most interesting things that Jimmy Iovine told me, we talked a lot about this, because I'm obsessed with people that are just further down the line than I am.
sentences.zh: Jimmy Iovine 告诉过我一件最有趣的事，我们经常谈论这个，因为我痴迷于那些比我走得更远的人。

sentences.en: There's just the wisdom they gain from experience.
sentences.zh: 他们从经验中获得的智慧是无可替代的。

sentences.en: I got the book knowledge. I need the stuff that's not in there that they can tell you.
sentences.zh: 我有书本知识。我需要的是那些书里没有的、他们能告诉我的东西。

sentences.en: And he was just like, most people cannot handle.
sentences.zh: 他当时就说，大多数人都无法承受。

sentences.en: You guys have been around some of the most talented people, genius level talents that have completely imploded maybe destroyed their lives maybe died prematurely and so he broke it down like four things for me like there's like people can't help stress and these are the pitfalls david that you should watch out for one was drugs second was alcohol third was women and fourth was megalomania that you know it's really hard to get on stage and there's 80 000 people screaming your name and over time they just think there's some kind of they're not even human anymore which you seem to be like i'm not special i have no i know you say you have no talent all this other shit but like i'm not special yeah i you know i think that's there's a lot of wisdom to that it's like man there's 10 million me's and 10 million you's all over the world or whatever that is do you think jimmy's perspective on that is like the people that you've seen that were had talent and had success and then destroyed it is there anything else that he's missing from there?
sentences.zh: 你们接触过一些最有天赋的人，那种天才级别的人，他们可能彻底崩溃了，可能毁了自己的人生，甚至过早离世。所以他给我总结了四点，他说这些是你要警惕的陷阱，David。第一是毒品，第二是酒精，第三是女人，第四是自大狂。你知道，站在舞台上，有八万人高喊你的名字，久而久之，他们甚至觉得自己不再是人类了。而你看起来好像是那种‘我不特别，我没天赋，我只是个普通人’的态度。是的，我认为这其中蕴含着很多智慧。就像是，伙计，全世界有千万个像我一样的人，也有千万个像你一样的人，或者诸如此类。你认为 Jimmy 对此的看法，也就是那些你见过的有天赋、获得成功却最终毁掉自己的人，他漏掉了什么吗？

sentences.en: I think those are all of them. It's like, because the last one takes into account a lot of like, there's both the mask of overconfidence and ego. which is hiding insecurity, or there's the insecurity.
sentences.zh: 我想这些就是全部了。因为最后一点涵盖了很多方面，既有过度自信和自负的面具，用来掩盖不安全感，也有纯粹的不安全感。

sentences.en: But they're really the same. You know, they're just presenting in two different ways.
sentences.zh: 但它们其实是一回事。你知道，它们只是以两种不同的方式呈现出来。

sentences.en: Two different people have the same overnight success.
sentences.zh: 两个人经历了同样的一夜成名。

sentences.en: One of them gets really boastful and I'm the greatest that ever lived.
sentences.zh: 其中一个变得非常自夸，说‘我是有史以来最伟大的’。

sentences.en: And the other one is like, oh my God, they're going to find out that I'm really a fake.
sentences.zh: 而另一个则觉得，‘天哪，他们会发现我其实是个骗子’。

sentences.en: But those are both the same people. It's the same.
sentences.zh: 但他们其实是同一种人。是一样的。

sentences.en: They're two sides of the same coin. The megalomania is a way of hiding the insecurity.
sentences.zh: 它们是同一枚硬币的两面。自大狂是一种掩盖不安全感的方式。

sentences.en: It's a brave face. They might not know this.
sentences.zh: 这是一种勇敢的伪装。他们可能自己都没意识到。

sentences.en: They rarely know it, you know. It's different sides of the same imbalance.
sentences.zh: 他们很少意识到这一点。这是同一种失衡的不同侧面。

sentences.en: So that leads me to the question I hinted at or maybe even said, like, how do you sustain success over such a long period of time then?
sentences.zh: 那么这引出了我之前暗示过，或者可能已经说出的问题：你是如何能在如此长的时间里保持成功的？

sentences.en: I think the fact that I learned to meditate when I was young and always had a grounded, and the fact that I know it's not me.
sentences.zh: 我想是因为我年轻时学会了冥想，而且一直保持着脚踏实地，再加上我知道这一切并不是因为我个人。

sentences.en: It's like those two things. I'm grounded, and I know I'm lucky to participate in this magic that's happening.
sentences.zh: 就是这两点。我保持清醒，而且我知道我很幸运能参与到这种正在发生的魔力之中。

sentences.en: I get to be in the room when it happens, but it's not from me.
sentences.zh: 我有幸在事情发生时身处现场，但它并非源于我。

sentences.en: What do you mean it's not from you? I'm in the service of it.
sentences.zh: 你说的‘并非源于你’是什么意思？我是为它服务的。

sentences.en: You're like a conduit? What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你就像一个管道？你的意思是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, I would say that. I'm in the service of it.
sentences.zh: 是的，我会这么说。我是为它服务的。

sentences.en: I'm devoted to setting the stage to allow it to happen.
sentences.zh: 我致力于搭建舞台，让它能够发生。

sentences.en: And I'm patient and waiting for it to come.
sentences.zh: 我很有耐心，等待它的到来。

sentences.en: It's not like when it's great, it's like I did a great job.
sentences.zh: 并不是说当事情做得很好时，我就觉得‘我做得真棒’。

sentences.en: It's not that. No, I think the people that sustain greatness over time, even if they do something great, they don't like rest on their laurels.
sentences.zh: 不是那样的。不，我认为那些能长期保持卓越的人，即使他们做出了伟大的成就，也不会躺在功劳簿上睡大觉。

sentences.en: They don't go to sleep on wins. They just make something great.
sentences.zh: 他们不会沉溺于胜利。他们只是继续创造伟大的作品。

sentences.en: They're like, all right, do try to do it again the next day.
sentences.zh: 他们会想，‘好吧，明天再试着做一次’。

sentences.en: And they don't really think too much. uh jimmy i've been has i keep bringing him up but uh he has that great line where he's just like i don't have a rear view mirror and i don't have a trophy room yeah just like i don't give it even when he did the show he's like i don't want to talk about the past i want to talk about like what i'm working on in the future they're all like that i just had lunch with jeffrey katzenberg same thing he's just like yeah we do the show but like i want to talk about what i'm working on now not just what happened at disney and everything else it's just very very common uh like staying in the moment being present i let me tell me if you disagree with me uh because again like i have this interpretation of you in my mind because i've been a fan of yours for a very long time and going back to this sustained success over a long period of time.
sentences.zh: 他们其实不会想太多。Jimmy Iovine——我一直提到他——他有一句名言，他说‘我没有后视镜，也没有陈列室’。是的，就像我根本不在乎。即使他做那个节目时，他也说‘我不想谈论过去，我想谈论我未来正在做的事情’。他们都是这样。我刚和 Jeffrey Katzenberg 吃过午饭，也是一样。他就像是‘是的，我们做了那个节目，但我现在想谈谈我正在做的事情，而不是仅仅谈论在 Disney 发生过的一切’。这非常非常普遍。就像活在当下，保持专注。让我告诉你，如果你不同意我的看法请直说，因为我脑海中对你有一个解读，因为我做你的粉丝很久了，回到这个长期保持成功的话题。

sentences.en: I talked to James Dyson, the guy that invented the vacuum cleaner guy.
sentences.zh: 我和 James Dyson 聊过，就是发明吸尘器的那个人。

sentences.en: And he's a fascinating person to me. Number one person I wanted to meet because his first autobiography, I think is so great because it's all about him just enduring to struggle and refuse to quit.
sentences.zh: 他对我来说是一个迷人的人。他是我想见的第一人，因为他的第一本自传我觉得非常棒，因为它讲的全是他如何忍受挣扎并拒绝放弃。

sentences.en: And something I didn't understand, even though I read his first autobiography five times, second autobiography two or three times and his encyclopedia, he wrote an encyclopedia.
sentences.zh: 有些事情我没理解，尽管我读了他的第一本自传五遍，第二本两三遍，还有他的百科全书，他写过一本百科全书。

sentences.en: This, I love obsessed people. He's an inventor.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢痴迷的人。他是一位发明家。

sentences.en: He wrote an encyclopedia while he's building his company on a history of great inventions.
sentences.zh: 他在建立公司时写了一本关于伟大发明历史的百科全书。

sentences.en: And he's like fucking 200 inventions in there.
sentences.zh: 里面有大概 200 项发明。

sentences.en: He's like, look at this little weird thing.
sentences.zh: 他会说，‘看看这个奇怪的小东西’。

sentences.en: And he's just like complete. Obsessed. Obsessed.
sentences.zh: 他就是完全的痴迷。痴迷。

sentences.en: But what I didn't understand what was driving him was he told me this great story on the podcast where he goes, this is his simple organizing principle.
sentences.zh: 但我没理解是什么在驱动他。他在播客里给我讲了一个很棒的故事，他说，这是他简单的组织原则。

sentences.en: He's like, I pick up a product, right? Cop, pick up a product, it exists.
sentences.zh: 他说，我拿起一个产品，对吧？拿起一个产品，它已经存在了。

sentences.en: I go, how can I make this product better?
sentences.zh: 我说，我怎样才能让这个产品更好？

sentences.en: Makes it better, puts it back down. Waits a little bit, picks it up.
sentences.zh: 改进它，把它放回去。等一会儿，再把它拿起来。

sentences.en: Goes, how can I make it better? Makes it better, puts it down.
sentences.zh: 说，我怎样才能让它更好？改进它，放回去。

sentences.en: He goes, I just do that over and over again.
sentences.zh: 他说，我就这样一遍又一遍地做。

sentences.en: Yeah. I've been doing it for 50 years. So if I had to guess what your organizing principle was, that I think also influences the sustained success that you've had, is you just making things that you yourself like.
sentences.zh: 是的。我已经这样做了 50 年了。所以如果我要猜你的组织原则是什么，我认为这也影响了你所取得的持续成功，那就是你只是在制作你自己喜欢的东西。

sentences.en: That's it. And sometimes I'll go into a friend's house and I'll think the furniture in here isn't arranged in the best way.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。有时我会去朋友家，我会觉得那里的家具摆放得不是最好的方式。

sentences.en: Maybe I'll rearrange the furniture. No, you don't.
sentences.zh: 也许我会重新摆放家具。不，你不会吧。

sentences.en: I've done that. I've done that. What does your friend say?
sentences.zh: 我做过。我做过。你朋友怎么说？

sentences.en: Depends. Some are cool with it, some are like he's crazy.
sentences.zh: 看情况。有的觉得没问题，有的觉得他疯了。

sentences.en: Okay, we could say more about this. Well, it's just like seeing the possibility.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们可以多聊聊这个。嗯，这就像是看到可能性。

sentences.en: I've worked on a lot of living spaces, and the idea of designing a house from scratch is a daunting one to me.
sentences.zh: 我参与过很多居住空间的设计，从零开始设计房子的想法对我来说很艰巨。

sentences.en: I can't imagine doing that because there's too many options.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象那样做，因为选择太多了。

sentences.en: But if there's a house that exists, I might be able to see, well, what's the best version of this thing that already exists.
sentences.zh: 但如果房子已经存在，我或许能看出，‘这个现有的东西，最好的版本是什么样的’。

sentences.en: And that's what's same. Same with music.
sentences.zh: 这就是同样的道理。音乐也是一样。

sentences.en: It's like, I hear what's there, and now what's the best version of this?
sentences.zh: 就像是，我听到了现有的东西，现在这个东西最好的版本是什么？

sentences.en: What can we do to make it better? What can we do to make it better?
sentences.zh: 我们能做些什么让它更好？我们能做些什么让它更好？

sentences.en: Same thing as James Dyson. Exactly the same.
sentences.zh: 和 James Dyson 一样。完全一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I feel like you did this from the jump when you were like, well, I'm in the club.
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得你从一开始就是这么做的，当时你说，‘好吧，我在俱乐部里’。

sentences.en: I'm obsessed going to the club. The hip-hop club is incredible, right?
sentences.zh: 我痴迷于去俱乐部。嘻哈俱乐部太棒了，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah. But I like this stuff that's here.
sentences.zh: 是的。但我喜欢这里的东西。

sentences.en: I go to the record store. I'm buying this stuff that I don't like.
sentences.zh: 我去唱片店。我买了一些我不喜欢的东西。

sentences.en: It's not real. Yeah. So I was like, why don't I just make what I actually like?
sentences.zh: 那不是真实的。是的。所以我当时想，为什么我不直接做我真正喜欢的东西呢？

sentences.en: Yeah. And it wound up working out like fabulously.
sentences.zh: 是的。结果它成功得不可思议。

sentences.en: But again, I didn't know in advance it would work out fabulously.
sentences.zh: 但同样，我事先并不知道它会成功得不可思议。

sentences.en: It's just like, this is what I want to hear.
sentences.zh: 这只是，这就是我想听到的。

sentences.en: I'm making it for me. Which these are my favorite kind of people because you're, again, it goes back to like, why are you doing what you're doing?
sentences.zh: 我是为自己而做的。而这些人是我最喜欢的一类人，因为这又回到了那个问题：你为什么要做你正在做的事情？

sentences.en: And you're doing it because you wanted to make it to the point where.
sentences.zh: 你做它是因为你想把它做到那个程度。

sentences.en: I want it in the world. You were willing to just make music at night and have a normal job just because you liked doing it.
sentences.zh: 我想让它出现在这个世界上。你愿意晚上做音乐，同时有一份正常的工作，仅仅因为你喜欢做这件事。

sentences.en: Absolutely. I never thought of any of this as a job.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。我从来没把这些当成一份工作。

sentences.en: It's never been about that. It's only a job because I'm committed to show up.
sentences.zh: 从来都不是为了那个。它之所以是工作，仅仅是因为我承诺要投入其中。

sentences.en: That's what makes it a job. The actual craft of making things is what I like to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是让它成为工作的原因。制作东西的实际工艺才是我喜欢做的。

sentences.en: What would have to happen for you to basically disappear and to stop working with musicians, stop making podcasts?
sentences.zh: 如果发生什么事，你会基本上消失，停止与音乐人合作，停止制作播客？

sentences.en: I think I would just keep making things for myself.
sentences.zh: 我想我还是会继续为自己制作东西。

sentences.en: You know, I give the example in the book of if you were to move into a house on the top of a mountain that no one could ever come and visit.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我在书里举过一个例子，如果你搬进山顶上的一所房子，没人能来拜访。

sentences.en: And you made that the place that you most wanted to spend your time and you really curated it to your taste.
sentences.zh: 你把它变成了你最想待的地方，并且完全按照你的品味来布置。

sentences.en: That's the job. It's not about I'm making this to show off to someone else.
sentences.zh: 那就是工作。并不是说我做这个是为了向别人炫耀。

sentences.en: I'm making this because I want to inhabit this.
sentences.zh: 我做这个是因为我想居住在其中。

sentences.en: I make the music that I want to, I'm excited to listen to.
sentences.zh: 我制作我想听的、让我感到兴奋的音乐。

sentences.en: Now, it's ridiculous. It doesn't work out that way because in making the music, we work on it.
sentences.zh: 现在，这很荒谬。事情并不是那样运作的，因为在制作音乐的过程中，我们一直在打磨它。

sentences.en: We listen to it a thousand times. And then when it's done, it's fine if I never hear it again.
sentences.zh: 我们听了一千遍。然后当它完成时，如果我再也不听它也没关系。

sentences.en: I never put on music I worked on, which is funny because I'm making it to be the perfect version of what I want to hear. but in the process of doing that there's so much listening involved that's not fun to go back and listen to it for me i want to hear something new this idea of the you the example that you use in the book of the house on the mountain that no one can ever see no one will ever see say more about the thinking behind that though well it's it's true i just know for me if i was i don't decorate my home to impress someone else.
sentences.zh: 我从不播放我制作过的音乐，这很有趣，因为我制作它是为了达到我想听到的完美版本。但在制作过程中，涉及了太多的聆听，对我来说，再回去听它已经不再有趣了。我想听点新的东西。关于你在书里用的那个‘山上的房子，没人能看见，没人会看见’的例子，能多说说背后的想法吗？嗯，这是真的，我只知道对我来说，如果我是……我装饰我的家不是为了给别人留下深刻印象。

sentences.en: I decorate my home to be the best version of the house that I want to live in.
sentences.zh: 我装饰我的家是为了让它成为我想居住的房子的最佳版本。

sentences.en: And it's not typical. I'm willing to go to extremes to make the thing that I want to inhabit.
sentences.zh: 而且它并不典型。我愿意走极端来打造我想要居住的东西。

sentences.en: And it's not for anyone else. It's just for me.
sentences.zh: 它不是为了任何人。它只是为了我。

sentences.en: Now, often other people, if they do happen to come over, they're like, wow, I'd love to live in a place like this.
sentences.zh: 现在，通常其他人如果碰巧过来，他们会说，‘哇，我真想住这样的地方’。

sentences.en: I've never been in a place like this. I think the metaphor that you're using there though, it's like a, almost like a, a map for people to find their life's work if they haven't found it yet.
sentences.zh: ‘我从来没去过这样的地方’。但我认为你用的那个比喻，就像是一张地图，指引人们去寻找他们的人生事业，如果他们还没找到的话。

sentences.en: It's like, what are you already doing? Yeah.
sentences.zh: 就像是，你已经在做什么了？是的。

sentences.en: And what will you do no matter what? What won't you stop doing regardless?
sentences.zh: 无论如何你都会做什么？无论如何你都不会停止做什么？

sentences.en: I always say it's like people say, oh, you know, if you love what you do, you would do it for free.
sentences.zh: 我总是说，人们会说，‘哦，你知道，如果你热爱你所做的事，你会免费去做’。

sentences.en: And I was like, no, there's another level to loving what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 而我会说，不，热爱你所做的事还有另一个层面。

sentences.en: If you truly love what you do, they couldn't pay you to stop.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的热爱你所做的事，他们花钱也无法让你停下来。

sentences.en: Yeah. I think it's excellent advice for helping people find their life's work.
sentences.zh: 是的。我认为这对帮助人们找到他们的人生事业来说是极好的建议。

sentences.en: Rick, this was awesome. You've been a huge inspiration to me.
sentences.zh: Rick，这太棒了。你一直是我巨大的灵感来源。

sentences.en: I've used a ton of your ideas in my work, and I hope this is the first conversation of many between me and you.
sentences.zh: 我在我的工作中用了你大量的想法，我希望这是我和你之间多次对话的第一次。

sentences.en: Great. Pleasure. Thanks for doing this. Thank you.
sentences.zh: 太好了。荣幸之至。谢谢你做这个。谢谢。

sentences.en: I hope you enjoyed this episode. Please remember to subscribe wherever you're listening and leave a review. and make sure you listen to my other podcast founders.
sentences.zh: 希望你喜欢这一期节目。请记得在你收听的地方订阅并留下评论。一定要去听我的另一个播客《Founders》。

sentences.en: For almost a decade, I've obsessively read over 400 biographies of history's greatest entrepreneurs searching for ideas that you can use in your work.
sentences.zh: 近十年来，我痴迷地阅读了 400 多本历史上最伟大企业家的传记，寻找你可以用在工作中的想法。

sentences.en: Most of the guests you hear on this show first found me through founders.
sentences.zh: 你在本节目中听到的大多数嘉宾，最初都是通过《Founders》找到我的。
